name: All Beer
description: Every recognized beer style, nested and grouped by similarity.

children.name: Ales
children.description: Top-fermented British, Irish, American and related ales (excluding Belgian, wheat, sour and hybrid styles): bitters, browns, pale ales, IPAs, porters, stouts and strong ales.

children.name: British Bitters & Pale Ales
children.description: Amber-to-gold English session ales built on pale ale malt, English hops and fruity British yeast; traditionally served on cask.

children.name: Ordinary Bitter
children.description: Low-gravity, easy-drinking cask bitter with moderate bitterness, bready/biscuity malt, light caramel and earthy-floral English hops.
malts: Touch of amber or dark malt for colour
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

parents.note: BJCP: the family of British bitters grew out of English pale ales as a draught product after the late 1800s.

notes.aroma: Bready, biscuity malt with a touch of caramel, mild fruit and earthy or floral English hops.
notes.flavor: Bitter-leaning but balanced: biscuit malt, light esters and earthy hops, finishing dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body with low, soft carbonation; built for easy pints.

children.tryIf: you want a low-alcohol pub pint with real flavor and a dry, bitter finish

children.name: Best Bitter
children.description: A step up in strength from ordinary bitter: balanced bitterness, toasty/caramel malt and English hop character, with fruity esters.
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

parents.note: BJCP: the British bitter family, of which best bitter is the standard-strength premium member, grew out of draught English pale ale after the late 1800s.

notes.aroma: Toasty, biscuity malt and light caramel with gentle fruit and earthy, floral English hops.
notes.flavor: Biscuit and toffee malt against firm bitterness, moderate esters and earthy hops; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body; low carbonation on cask, a bit livelier in the bottle.

children.tryIf: you like a classic English cask ale that balances malt and bitterness

children.name: Strong Bitter (ESB)
children.description: Stronger, fuller bitter (includes ESB) with richer caramel/toffee malt, firm bitterness and pronounced English hop and ester character.
malts: Touch of black malt for colour
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

parents.note: BJCP: strong bitters can be seen as a higher-gravity version of best bitters.
BJCP: bottled British pale ale roughly approximates a strong bitter (though historically the styles differed).

notes.aroma: Bready, nutty malt with caramel and marmalade-like fruit, plus floral or earthy hops.
notes.flavor: Rich biscuit and toffee malt with assertive bitterness, clear hop flavor and fruity esters.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body, low to moderate carbonation, sometimes a light alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like ESB-style ales with more malt, fruit and strength than a session bitter

children.name: English Pale Ale
children.description: Bottled/keg cousin of the bitters: golden-to-copper, biscuity malt, moderate earthy-herbal English hops; not a separate BJCP style (judged as bitter), defined by BA as Classic English-Style Pale Ale.
children.yeast: English ale yeast; Burton strains for sulfate-driven dryness
children.yearLabel: c.1700 (term 'pale ale' first recorded 1703); Burton pale ales 1820s–40s

notes.aroma: Bready malt with floral, herbal or earthy English hops and noticeable fruity esters.
notes.flavor: Even balance of light malt and medium bitterness, earthy hops and fruit, with a crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body with moderate carbonation; clean and crisp.

children.tryIf: you like balanced, fruity English ales with a crisp hoppy edge

children.name: British Golden Ale
children.description: Pale, refreshing hop-forward session ale created as a summer alternative to lager; clean malt canvas with citrusy or floral hops.
malts: Low-colour pale ale malt or lager malt

parents.note: BJCP: modern variants of bitter brewed exclusively with pale malt are known as golden ales, summer ales or golden bitters, developed to take on lager.

notes.aroma: Floral, herbal or citrusy hops over light bready malt; no caramel.
notes.flavor: Hop-forward and bitter with citrus or floral hop flavor, light bready malt and a dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body with low to moderate carbonation; refreshing.

children.tryIf: you like pale, hoppy, refreshing ales somewhere between a bitter and a pale ale

children.name: Australian Sparkling Ale
children.description: Bottle-conditioned, highly carbonated pale ale with fruity esters, bready malt and earthy-herbal Australian hops (Pride of Ringwood).
malts: Small amount of crystal for colour
children.yeast: Coopers-type Australian ale yeast, bottle conditioned

topSellers.name: Coopers Extra Strong Vintage Ale (stronger 7.5% variant, above style range)

parents.note: Bottled Australian ale was developed to compete with imported bottled British pale ales such as Bass.

notes.aroma: Soft pear and apple esters, earthy or herbal hops and grainy-bready malt; maybe a little sulfur.
notes.flavor: Smooth grainy malt, then firm bitterness, earthy-peppery hops and pome fruit; very dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body with very high, spritzy carbonation; crisp and gassy.

children.tryIf: you want a bitter, fizzy, thirst-quenching ale for hot weather, like Coopers Sparkling

children.name: Scottish & Irish Ales
children.description: Malt-forward, lightly hopped ales from Scotland and Ireland: clean, caramel-to-toasty, with dry roasty finishes in the Irish red.

children.name: Scottish Light (60/-)
children.description: Very low-strength, malt-focused dark amber ale with light caramel, toast and a dry, slightly roasty finish; minimal hops.
malts: Small amount of roasted barley or black malt
children.yearLabel: post-WWII modern form (shilling names used earlier for mild ales)

parents.note: Pattinson: the post-WWII 60/-, 70/- and 80/- beers were Scottish draught pale ales of three strengths, often parti-gyled, unrelated to older beers with the same shilling names.

notes.aroma: Caramel, toffee and toasted-bread malt with a hint of butterscotch and light fruit.
notes.flavor: Toasty caramel malt with just enough bitterness to avoid cloying; slight roasty dryness at the end.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-low to medium body, low to moderate carbonation, sometimes lightly creamy.

children.tryIf: you want a gentle, malty, very low-alcohol session beer

children.name: Scottish Heavy (70/-)
children.description: Session-strength amber Scottish ale: caramel, toasted malt and a dry finish, with very low hop character.
malts: Small amount of roasted barley or black malt
children.yearLabel: post-WWII modern form (shilling names used earlier for mild ales)

parents.note: Pattinson: the post-WWII 60/-, 70/- and 80/- beers were Scottish draught pale ales of three strengths, often parti-gyled, unrelated to older beers with the same shilling names.

notes.aroma: Toffee and caramel malt with graham-cracker toastiness and a whisper of fruit.
notes.flavor: Malty and toasty with caramel overtones, low bitterness and a slightly roasty, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-low to medium body; low to moderate carbonation, smooth and lightly creamy.

children.tryIf: you like malty amber ales and want something easygoing and low in bitterness

children.name: Scottish Export (80/-)
children.description: The strongest of the session Scottish ales: richer caramel, toffee and toasted malt with a clean, dry finish.
malts: Small amount of roasted barley or black malt
children.yearLabel: post-WWII modern form (shilling names used earlier for mild ales)

parents.note: Pattinson: the post-WWII 60/-, 70/- and 80/- beers were Scottish draught pale ales of three strengths, often parti-gyled, unrelated to older beers with the same shilling names.

notes.aroma: Moderate caramel, toffee and toasted-biscuit malt with light fruit and faint earthy hops.
notes.flavor: Fuller toasty, caramel malt with modest bitterness and a light roasty dryness in the finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body with medium-low carbonation; smooth and sometimes creamy.

children.tryIf: you like malty, toffee-ish beers such as Belhaven-style Scottish ales

children.name: Irish Red Ale
children.description: Easy-drinking, clean red-amber ale with caramel/toffee sweetness up front and a dry, lightly roasted finish.

origin.era: 20th century (modern style adapted from English bitter); revived as a craft style

malts: Roasted barley (for colour and dry finish)
children.yearLabel: 20th century; 'Irish Red' popularised from 1981 (Killian's); a long earlier history is claimed but disputed

parents.note: BJCP: the modern style is essentially an adaptation of the popular English bitter, with less hopping and a little roasted barley for colour and dryness.

notes.aroma: Light caramel, toast and toffee malt over a clean, grainy base.
notes.flavor: Soft caramel and biscuit malt leading into a dry finish with a light roasted-grain bite.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate carbonation, smooth.

children.tryIf: you want an easy, slightly malty pint with a dry, toasty finish

children.name: Brown & Amber Ales
children.description: Caramel, nutty, toffee and chocolate-tinged ales from mild and brown ale traditions in Britain and their hoppier American descendants.

children.name: Dark Mild
children.description: Low-gravity, malt-driven dark ale with chocolate, caramel and light roast; soft body and very restrained hops.
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)
children.yearLabel: 1800s X ales; dark brown only after WWI

notes.aroma: Caramel, toffee, nutty and chocolate malt with light fruit; hops barely there.
notes.flavor: Malty with caramel, chocolate and light roast; low bitterness and a sweet-to-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body with low carbonation; feels fuller than its strength suggests.

children.tryIf: you want a dark, flavorful beer that is light in alcohol and easy to drink

children.name: British Brown Ale
children.description: Malty, caramel-nutty brown ale with toffee and light chocolate notes and moderate English hop bitterness.
malts: British mild or pale ale malt
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

notes.aroma: Sweet caramel and toffee malt with nutty and light chocolate notes; faint earthy hops.
notes.flavor: Nutty, toffee-like malt with gentle sweetness, medium-low bitterness and no real roast.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with medium to medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like nutty, caramel-forward beers such as Newcastle Brown Ale

children.name: London Brown Ale
children.description: Historical, very sweet, low-alcohol dark brown ale with caramel, toffee and dried-fruit flavours and minimal bitterness; often sweetened after fermentation.
malts: High proportion of dark crystal malt

topSellers.name: Forest Brown (historical; discontinued, no current third example)

notes.aroma: Rich caramel and toffee sweetness with plummy dark fruit.
notes.flavor: Deep toffee-sweet malt with hints of biscuit and coffee; low bitterness and a sweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body that feels heavier from the sweetness; creamy and smooth.

children.tryIf: you like sweet, toffee-rich dark beers with very little bitterness or alcohol

children.name: American Brown Ale
children.description: Malty, chocolate-caramel brown ale with more bitterness and citrusy/piney American hop character than its British parent.

parents.note: Pete Slosberg's Pete's Wicked Ale (1986) grew out of his homebrew attempts to copy Samuel Smith's Nut Brown Ale.

notes.aroma: Chocolate, caramel and nutty-toasty malt, often with citrusy or earthy American hops.
notes.flavor: Chocolate and caramel malt balanced by medium bitterness and clear American hop flavor.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body, moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like brown ales but want more hop character and a chocolatey edge

children.name: American Amber / Red Ale
children.description: Amber-to-red ale balancing caramel malt sweetness with citrusy, piney American hops; includes most American 'red ales'.

parents.note: BJCP: developed as a variation from American Pale Ales.
Early US microbreweries brewed amber-coloured ESBs, and Full Sail's brewmaster called English ESB the source material for American amber.

notes.aroma: Caramel malt with citrusy, piney or floral American hops.
notes.flavor: Malty-sweet caramel up front, moderate to high hop flavor and a firm bitter, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body, medium to high carbonation, smooth.

children.tryIf: you want caramel malt and American hops in roughly equal measure

children.name: American Pale & Blonde Ales
children.description: Pale, clean American ales: hop-led pale ales and soft, approachable blonde ales.

children.name: American Pale Ale
children.description: Pale, refreshing, hop-forward ale with citrus/pine American hops over a clean, lightly bready malt base; the beer that launched US craft.

parents.note: BJCP: a modern American craft-era adaptation of English pale ale using indigenous ingredients.

notes.aroma: Citrus, pine, floral or tropical American hops over light grainy or bready malt.
notes.flavor: Hop-forward with bright hop flavor and firm bitterness on a clean, light malt base; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate to high carbonation, no harshness.

children.tryIf: you want a hoppy, balanced craft beer that is less intense than an IPA

children.name: Blonde Ale
children.description: Easy-drinking, pale golden craft ale with soft bready malt, light fruity or floral hops and a clean finish; a craft 'gateway' beer.
children.yeast: Clean American ale yeast, Kölsch or lager yeast

parents.note: BJCP: produced as a faster-produced ale alternative to standard American lagers, first believed brewed at Catamount in 1987.

notes.aroma: Light grainy-bready malt with a gentle touch of citrus, floral or fruity hops.
notes.flavor: Soft, clean malt with light hop flavor and low-medium bitterness; balanced toward the malt.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with lively carbonation; smooth and easy.

children.tryIf: you are new to craft beer or want something light, clean and crowd-pleasing

children.name: IPAs
children.description: India Pale Ales and their many modern variants: hop-forward, bitter-to-juicy pale ales.

children.name: IPA (India Pale Ale)
children.description: Hop-forward pale ale family, from earthy English originals to resinous West Coast, juicy hazy and strong double versions; IPA is roughly half of US craft off-premise dollar sales. Ranges shown span the BJCP-defined IPA styles (12C, 21A-C, 22A); session and triple IPAs fall outside them.
children.yeast: Clean American or attenuative English ale yeast

children.name: English IPA
children.description: Hoppy, moderately strong pale ale with earthy, floral and marmalade English hops, biscuity malt and a dry finish.

parents.note: BJCP: the East India Company had Allsopp recreate and reformulate the London pale stock ale in Burton in 1823; White Shield traces to 1829.

notes.aroma: Floral, spicy-peppery or orange-citrus English hops over bready, biscuity malt.
notes.flavor: Assertive bitterness and earthy-floral hop flavor with bready, lightly toasty malt; dry, minerally finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate to lively carbonation; smooth.

children.tryIf: you like IPAs but prefer earthy, marmalade-like English hops over citrus bombs

children.name: American IPA
children.description: Decidedly hoppy and bitter pale ale with citrus, pine, resin and tropical American hops over a clean, dry malt base.

parents.note: BJCP: the first modern American craft adaptation of the traditional English style, using whole Cascade hops.

notes.aroma: Intense American hops (citrus, pine, resin, tropical or stone fruit) over clean, grainy malt.
notes.flavor: Big hop flavor with medium-high to very high bitterness, lean malt and a dry, bitter finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, medium carbonation, smooth with no harshness.

children.tryIf: you want the classic hop-forward, bitter craft IPA

children.name: West Coast IPA
children.description: Bone-dry, crystal-clear, very bitter IPA showcasing piney, resinous and citrus hops over a minimal pale malt base; BA-recognised separately since 2023 (BJCP judges it as American IPA).
children.yeast: Clean, highly attenuative American ale yeast (Chico)

parents.note: BJCP: dry, sharply bitter, clear examples known as West Coast IPA are really just a type of American IPA; refined in 1990s Southern California.

notes.aroma: Loud pine, resin, citrus and dank hop aromas with very little malt.
notes.flavor: Intense hop flavor and firm, clean bitterness over a lean malt base; crisp, bone-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body, brisk carbonation; highly attenuated and crisp.

children.tryIf: you like clear, dry, piney IPAs with a serious bitter snap

children.name: Hazy IPA (New England IPA)
children.description: Opaque, soft and juicy IPA with intense tropical/stone-fruit hop aroma, low perceived bitterness and a creamy, full mouthfeel.
children.yeast: Estery English or American ale yeast (e.g. London Ale III), with biotransformation dry hopping

parents.note: BJCP: originated in New England as an American IPA variant; Heady Topper the original inspiration.

notes.aroma: Intense juicy hops (mango, passion fruit, citrus, stone fruit) over soft, bready malt.
notes.flavor: Juicy, fruity hop flavor with low-to-medium perceived bitterness and a soft, off-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body, smooth and silky; medium carbonation.

children.tryIf: you love tropical-fruit hop flavor but don't want a harsh bitter bite

children.name: Double IPA (Imperial IPA)
children.description: Intensely hoppy, strong, dry IPA with big citrus/pine/tropical hop flavour, high bitterness and a clean, sugar-lightened body.

origin.era: Mid-late 1990s (Vinnie Cilurzo's Inaugural Ale at Blind Pig, 1994; popularised by Pliny the Elder, 2000)

children.yearLabel: 1994 (Blind Pig Inaugural Ale); Pliny the Elder 2000

parents.note: BJCP: an American craft innovation of the mid-late 1990s as a more intense version of American IPA.

notes.aroma: Intense, layered hops (citrus, pine, resin, tropical) with a hint of clean alcohol.
notes.flavor: Huge hop flavor and high bitterness over soft, light malt; dry finish, never sweet or heavy.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth, with restrained alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a bigger, stronger, hoppier IPA that still drinks clean

children.name: Triple IPA
children.description: An informal super-strong extension of the double IPA, roughly 10% ABV and up, with enormous hop saturation and a still-dry finish; not recognised by BJCP or BA.

parents.note: Pliny the Younger was conceived as an amped-up version of the double IPA Pliny the Elder.

notes.aroma: Massive resinous, citrus and tropical hop aroma with noticeable alcohol.
notes.flavor: Saturated hop flavor and very high bitterness, with a bit more malt sweetness and warming alcohol.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body with clear alcohol warmth; smooth when fresh.

children.tryIf: you want the most extreme hop intensity and don't mind 10%+ alcohol

children.name: Session IPA
children.description: Lower-alcohol IPA (5% ABV or less; most commercial examples 3.5-5%) that keeps a full IPA hop aroma and bitterness in a light, dry body; BJCP judges it as a session-strength 21B Specialty IPA, and BA sets the floor at 0.5% ABV.
malts: Light crystal or dextrin malt for body

parents.note: BJCP: a Session IPA is a 21B Specialty IPA with American IPA as its base style, brewed at session strength.

notes.aroma: Bright, punchy hops (citrus, tropical, pine) on a very light malt base.
notes.flavor: IPA-style hop flavor and medium-high bitterness with less malt and alcohol; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body, lively carbonation; crisp and easy.

children.tryIf: you want IPA hop flavor in a beer you can drink a few of

children.name: Black IPA (Cascadian Dark Ale)
children.description: Black-coloured IPA: American IPA hop intensity with light, dry roast from debittered dark malt and little burnt character.

origin.era: c. 1990 (Greg Noonan's Blackwatch IPA, Vermont Pub & Brewery); popular early 2010s

children.yearLabel: c.1990 (Greg Noonan's Blackwatch IPA); fad early 2010s

parents.note: BJCP: an American IPA variant first commercially produced by Greg Noonan around 1990.

notes.aroma: Pine, citrus and tropical hops with soft chocolate, coffee or toast in the background.
notes.flavor: Hop-forward and quite bitter, with restrained dark malt (light chocolate, never burnt); dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth, medium carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like IPAs and want a hint of dark-malt depth without a heavy stout

children.name: White IPA
children.description: Fruity, spicy, refreshing cross of a Belgian witbier and an American IPA: wheat body, Belgian yeast spice and citrusy hops.

parents.note: BJCP: a craft interpretation of American IPA crossed with a Witbier.
Developed as a spring seasonal to appeal to Witbier and IPA drinkers alike.

notes.aroma: Orange, apricot and citrus esters with coriander or peppery spice and fruity hops.
notes.flavor: Fruity yeast and citrusy hops with a light spice note, light bready malt and high bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light body, medium to medium-high carbonation; dry and refreshing.

children.tryIf: you like witbier's orange-and-spice character but want IPA hops and bitterness

children.name: Red IPA
children.description: Hoppy, bitter, strong amber-red IPA where caramel and toffee malt support citrusy/piney American hops.

parents.note: BJCP: based on American IPA but with the malt flavours of an American Amber Ale.
BJCP: Red Tail-style amber ales were the progenitor of Red IPAs.

notes.aroma: Citrus, pine or tropical hops with caramel, toffee and toasted-bread malt.
notes.flavor: Big hop flavor and firm bitterness over caramel and toffee malt; dry to medium finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth, medium to medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like American amber ales but want IPA-level hops and bitterness

children.name: Rye IPA
children.description: American IPA with a generous portion of rye malt adding a dry, spicy, grainy edge to the hop character.

topSellers.name: Ruthless Rye IPA (historical; retired 2015, occasional small-batch revivals)

parents.note: BJCP: a modern craft-era variation of American IPA, popular among homebrewers.

notes.aroma: Intense citrus, pine or tropical hops with a light peppery rye note.
notes.flavor: Hop-forward and very bitter, with spicy, grainy rye adding to a dry, crisp finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with a smooth, slightly creamy texture from the rye.

children.tryIf: you like American IPAs and enjoy a peppery, rye-bread edge

children.name: Brown IPA
children.description: Hoppy, bitter brown ale: chocolate and caramel malt flavours with American IPA hop intensity and dryness.
children.yearLabel: 1980s–90s homebrew 'Texas brown'; Dogfish Head Indian Brown 1999

parents.note: BJCP: the hoppier, stronger homebrew-era American browns are now classed as Brown IPA.
Brewed to IPA strength and hopping (Dogfish Head calls Indian Brown the prototypical dark IPA).

notes.aroma: Citrus, pine or tropical hops mingled with milk chocolate, toffee, nuts and toast.
notes.flavor: Hoppy and firmly bitter, with chocolate, caramel and nutty malt nearly in balance; dryish finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with a smooth texture.

children.tryIf: you like American brown ales and want them hopped like an IPA

children.name: Belgian IPA
children.description: IPA fermented with Belgian Tripel/golden strong ale yeast: fruity-spicy phenolic yeast character, high carbonation and assertive hops.

parents.note: BJCP: homebrewers and craft brewers substituted Belgian yeast in their American IPA recipes.
BJCP: Belgian breweries added more hops to their stronger pale beers, and the style is a cross between an American IPA and a Belgian Tripel or Golden Strong Ale.

notes.aroma: Fruity Belgian yeast (pear, apple, citrus) and peppery spice alongside bright hops.
notes.flavor: Hops and Belgian yeast fruit-and-spice together, light malt, high bitterness and a dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body, lively carbonation, often a light alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like both Tripels and IPAs and want them in one glass

children.name: Brut IPA
children.description: Very pale, bone-dry, highly carbonated IPA fermented with amyloglucosidase enzyme; champagne-like, aromatic and low in bitterness. A 2018-19 fad that has largely disappeared from production.
malts: Pilsner or very pale base malt
children.yeast: Neutral ale yeast plus amyloglucosidase enzyme
adjuncts: Rice, corn or other adjuncts (up to 40%)

parents.note: BJCP: a west-coast reaction to hazy and milkshake IPAs, made bone-dry with enzymes.

notes.aroma: Bright tropical, stone-fruit and white-grape hops; the malt is barely noticeable.
notes.flavor: Big hop flavor with very low bitterness and almost no malt; bone-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Very light body with very high, Champagne-like carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want an IPA that drinks like sparkling wine: aromatic, bone-dry and fizzy

children.name: Cold IPA
children.description: 'Wester than West Coast' IPA: crisp, clear and dry, fermented warm with lager yeast and brewed with rice or corn, then heavily dry-hopped; not yet a BJCP or BA style.

parents.note: Kevin Davey's West Coast-style IPA brewed lager-style for a crisp, dry finish.
Uses the American adjunct-lager toolkit: 20–40% rice or corn in the grist and lager yeast (fermented warm).

notes.aroma: Intense, clean hop aroma (citrus, pine, tropical) with no yeast character and little malt.
notes.flavor: Bright hop flavor and firm, clean bitterness over a lean rice- or corn-lightened base; very dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body, high carbonation; crisp, lager-like snap.

children.tryIf: you like West Coast IPAs and crisp lagers and want both at once

children.yearLabel: late 1700s (Hodgson's pale ale to India by 1793; name 'IPA' c.1830s)

parents.note: A pale, well-hopped stock (October-type) ale shipped to India; Hodgson of Bow exported pale ale from at least 1793.

notes.aroma: Strong hop aroma (citrus, pine, tropical or floral, depending on type) over a light malt base.
notes.flavor: Hops lead with firm bitterness, light malt support and a dryish finish; varies by sub-style.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate carbonation; hazy versions are softer and fuller.

children.tryIf: you love hop aroma and a bitter bite

children.name: Porters & Stouts
children.description: Dark ales built on roasted, chocolate and brown malts, from London porter and dry Irish stout to sweet, tropical and imperial strengths.

children.name: English Porter
children.description: Moderate-strength brown-to-black London ale with chocolate, toffee and bready brown-malt flavours and gentle roast.
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

notes.aroma: Bready, toasty malt with mild chocolate roast, caramel, nuts and toffee.
notes.flavor: Chocolate and toffee malt with gentle roast, never burnt; balanced bitterness and a dryish finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate carbonation, lightly creamy.

children.tryIf: you like chocolatey dark beers that stay gentle and sessionable

children.name: American Porter
children.description: Robust, roasty dark ale with chocolate and coffee malt, more bitterness and American hop character than English porter.
children.yeast: Clean American or characterful English ale yeast

parents.note: BJCP: a stronger, more aggressive version of earlier Pre-Prohibition Porters...
...or English Porters, first brewed in the modern craft beer era.

notes.aroma: Chocolate and light coffee roast with caramel and resiny or earthy hops.
notes.flavor: Moderately strong chocolatey roast with medium-high bitterness and hop flavor; dry to medium-sweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full body, moderate carbonation; slight dark-malt grip.

children.tryIf: you like dark chocolate and coffee notes with a hoppier, more bitter edge

children.name: Baltic Porter
children.description: Strong, smooth dark beer with dark fruit, caramel, toffee and chocolate; usually lager-fermented (grouped here with porters by lineage, though BJCP places it in 9 Strong European Beer).

origin.country: Baltic region (Poland, Finland, Russia, Baltic states)

topSellers.name: Baltika No. 6 Porter
topSellers.brewery: Baltika (VG Invest since Dec 2024; formerly Carlsberg)

parents.note: BJCP: developed in Baltic countries after imports of English porter were interrupted in the early 1800s, later adapted to bottom fermentation; English porter was the parent of such regional interpretations.
BJCP: the strong English export stouts were, with porter, the imports that Baltic brewers set out to replace in the early 1800s.

notes.aroma: Rich caramel, toffee and licorice malt with plums, raisins and a hint of chocolate.
notes.flavor: Malty-sweet start turning to smooth, lager-like roast and dried fruit; dryish finish, no burnt edge.
notes.mouthfeel: Full and smooth with deceptive, well-aged alcohol warmth; medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like rich, strong dark beers that are smooth rather than harsh

children.name: Pre-Prohibition Porter
children.description: Historical American porter: lighter-bodied, low roast, often brewed with lager yeast and adjuncts such as corn, molasses or porterine.
malts: Low percentages of black, chocolate and brown malt
children.yearLabel: 19th century (porter brewed in Philadelphia from the 1770s; lager methods after 1850)

parents.note: BJCP: brewed in Philadelphia from the revolutionary period as an adaptation of English beer, later modified by German immigrant lager brewers.

notes.aroma: Grainy malt with light chocolate, caramel, licorice and burnt-sugar notes; clean.
notes.flavor: Grainy-bready malt with low chocolate and burnt-sugar flavors, even bitterness and a dryish finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, moderate carbonation, lightly creamy.

children.tryIf: you want a lighter, crisper, lager-like take on porter

children.name: Irish Stout
children.description: Black, dry, roasty stout with coffee-like roasted barley, firm bitterness and a creamy (often nitro) body; low alcohol.
children.yearLabel: c.1810 (Guinness 'stouter kind of porter'); diverged late 1800s

parents.note: BJCP: evolved from London porters; Guinness brewed only porter from 1799 and a stouter porter from around 1810.

notes.aroma: Coffee-like roasted barley up front with hints of dark chocolate and cocoa.
notes.flavor: Roasty, coffee-like and dry, with medium-high bitterness and bittersweet chocolate.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, creamy (especially on nitro), low carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like black coffee and a dry, roasty pint like Guinness

children.name: Irish Extra Stout
children.description: Fuller, stronger bottled Irish stout with more roast, chocolate and coffee depth and a dry, bitter finish.

parents.note: BJCP: same roots as Irish Stout but a stronger, mainly bottled product.

notes.aroma: Coffee and roasted grain with dark chocolate, cocoa and a hint of biscuit.
notes.flavor: Pronounced coffee-and-chocolate roast with medium-high bitterness and some malty richness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body, creamy and very smooth, slightly warming.

children.tryIf: you like Irish stout but want it fuller and richer

children.name: Sweet / Milk Stout
children.description: Full-bodied, sweet, creamy stout with milk-chocolate and coffee flavours; residual sweetness usually from lactose.

parents.note: BJCP calls porter the predecessor of all stouts; sweet (milk) stout was an English stout of the early 1900s sweetened with lactose.

notes.aroma: Mild roast with coffee and chocolate and a creamy, sweet impression.
notes.flavor: Sweetened coffee and milk chocolate; roast and moderate bitterness offset by lasting sweetness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body, creamy, with low to moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like sweet coffee drinks or milk chocolate

children.name: Oatmeal Stout
children.description: Smooth, silky dark stout where oats add body and a nutty, grainy depth to coffee and chocolate roast.

parents.note: BJCP calls porter the predecessor of all stouts; oatmeal stout arose around 1900 as a nourishing stout made with oats.

notes.aroma: Coffee-and-cream roast with light malty sweetness and a grainy, nutty oat note.
notes.flavor: Mild coffee and milk chocolate with nutty oats, medium bitterness and a medium finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body, silky and velvety from the oats; creamy.

children.tryIf: you want a smooth, silky stout that is neither too bitter nor too sweet

children.name: Tropical Stout
children.description: Sweet, fruity, strong stout popular in the Caribbean and Asia: smooth roast, high esters and clean sugar-boosted strength.
children.yearLabel: 20th century (date approx.; e.g. Dragon Stout, Jamaica, 1920s)

parents.note: BJCP: a local adaptation of Foreign Extra Stouts brewed with indigenous ingredients in the Caribbean and other tropical markets.

notes.aroma: Sweet coffee and chocolate roast with molasses, dark-rum notes and plenty of fruit.
notes.flavor: Quite sweet, with smooth non-burnt roast, high fruity esters and a molasses-like edge.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body, creamy, with gentle alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like sweet, fruity, rum-like flavors in a stout (think Lion Stout)

children.name: Foreign Extra Stout
children.description: Strong, roasty, export-strength stout with coffee, chocolate and dark-fruit notes and firm bitterness; dominant in Africa and the Caribbean.

parents.note: BJCP: stronger, more heavily hopped export stouts (stout porters) of the 18th–19th centuries; Guinness' West India Porter of 1801 became Foreign Extra Stout.

notes.aroma: Strong coffee and dark-chocolate roast with some molasses, licorice or dried fruit.
notes.flavor: Bold roast and solid bitterness with hints of dark fruit, finishing fairly dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body, smooth, with a gentle warming alcohol presence.

children.tryIf: you like Irish stout and want a stronger, bolder, more bitter version

children.name: American Stout
children.description: Roasty, bitter, full-flavoured stout with coffee and dark chocolate and often noticeable American hop character.

parents.note: BJCP: applied aggressive American hopping to a strong traditional English or Irish stout.

notes.aroma: Strong coffee and dark-chocolate roast with citrusy or resiny American hops.
notes.flavor: Heavily roasted coffee and bittersweet chocolate with firm bitterness and hop flavor; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full body, can be creamy, fairly high carbonation, light warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a bold, roasty stout with a hoppy American kick

children.name: Imperial Stout
children.description: Intensely flavoured, big, dark ale with deep roast, dark fruit, chocolate and warming alcohol; ranges from British fruity-malty to American roasty-hoppy.
children.yeast: English or American ale yeast (alcohol tolerant)

children.name: American Imperial Stout
children.description: Big, roasty, intensely bitter imperial stout with more pronounced roast, hop bitterness and often American hop aroma than British versions.

parents.note: BJCP: embraced in the US craft era as an adaptation extending the style with American hops and roast.

notes.aroma: Intense roast, dark chocolate and coffee with bold American hops and evident alcohol.
notes.flavor: Huge, sweet malt and roast matched by high bitterness and citrusy or piney hop flavor.
notes.mouthfeel: Full and chewy with clear alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want the biggest, boldest, hoppiest version of a dark beer

children.name: British Imperial Stout
children.description: The original 'Russian' imperial stout: rich dark fruit, treacle and chocolate with balanced roast, fruity esters and moderate bitterness.

origin.era: Late 18th century (Thrale's/Barclay Perkins for the Russian court)

children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

parents.note: BJCP: the English strand of the style all but died out and was revived in the craft era as an export.

notes.aroma: Toffee, caramel and dark dried fruit with moderate roast and hints of chocolate.
notes.flavor: Very rich caramel-toffee malt and dark-fruit esters with gentler roast; bitterness supports, never dominates.
notes.mouthfeel: Full, smooth and warming.

children.tryIf: you want a strong, rich stout that leans fruity and malty rather than hoppy or harsh

children.yearLabel: 1780s (Thrale's strong export stout for the Russian court)

parents.note: BJCP: traces roots to strong English porters brewed for export in the 1700s; stouts were originally called 'stout porters'.

notes.aroma: Deep roast, dark chocolate and coffee layered with dried dark fruit and warming alcohol.
notes.flavor: Intense roast and chocolate over rich malt; strong bitterness balances the sweetness; warming finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Full to very full, velvety and chewy; low to moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like espresso, dark chocolate and big, warming beers

children.name: Pastry Stout
children.description: Strong, very sweet dessert-like stout flavoured to evoke pastries and confections (vanilla, chocolate, maple, coconut, fruit), often with lactose; judged under BA's 'Dessert or Pastry Beer' (2026; 'Dessert Stout or Pastry Stout' from 2023), whose colour range runs 13-40+ SRM, stouts being the dark end.

parents.note: Usually built on an imperial stout base loaded with dessert adjuncts (lactose, vanilla, cacao, etc.).

notes.aroma: Dessert-like: chocolate, vanilla, coffee, maple, coconut or marshmallow over rich roast (varies).
notes.flavor: Very sweet and rich, with dessert flavors on a roasty imperial stout base and little bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Very full, thick and syrupy-smooth with noticeable alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a beer that tastes like dessert: brownies, s'mores or tiramisu

children.name: Strong Ales
children.description: High-gravity British and American ales: malty, warming and often aged, from old ales and wee heavies to barleywines and wheatwines.

children.name: British Strong Ale
children.description: Malty, fruity, warming ale above bitter strength, with caramel, toffee and dried-fruit flavours; broad catch-all for strong British ales.
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

notes.aroma: Malty-sweet with caramel, toffee, nuts and dried fruit, plus soft alcohol.
notes.flavor: Rich nutty, toffee malt and dried-fruit esters, evident strength, and a medium-dry to sweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full body, chewy and smooth; alcohol warmth evident.

children.tryIf: you like rich, warming English ales but want something less intense than barleywine

children.name: Old Ale
children.description: Strong, malty ale showing aged character: dark fruit, toffee, sherry-like oxidation and sometimes light tartness or Brett.
children.yeast: Characterful British ale yeast (e.g. London/Fuller's, Whitbread or Yorkshire strains)

notes.aroma: Malty-sweet with dried fruit, molasses, toffee and treacle; aged versions show sherry or port notes.
notes.flavor: Luscious nutty, caramel malt and dark-fruit esters with evident alcohol; aged examples turn vinous.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full and chewy, warming; older examples are thinner, sometimes lightly tart or tannic.

children.tryIf: you enjoy sherry, port or aged spirits and like beers that change with age

children.name: Wee Heavy (Strong Scotch Ale)
children.description: Rich, malty, caramel-forward strong Scottish ale with toffee, plum and a full, sweet body; hops very restrained.
children.yearLabel: late 1700s–1800s Edinburgh ales; 'Wee Heavy' name from Fowler's

notes.aroma: Strong caramel, toffee and toasty malt with butterscotch-like sweetness, dried fruit and alcohol.
notes.flavor: Rich, sweet caramel-toffee malt with plum and raisin hints, low bitterness and a whisper of roast.
notes.mouthfeel: Full, thick and chewy with a smooth, warming alcohol glow.

children.tryIf: you like caramel, toffee and big, warming beers by the fire

children.name: English Barley Wine
children.description: Very strong, complex, malt-rich ale with dark fruit, toffee and caramel and a balanced, often aged, warming finish.

origin.era: 18th–19th century; term popularised by Bass No. 1 (1870s)

children.yearLabel: 1872 (Bass No. 1 first called a barley wine)

parents.note: BJCP: a modern descendant of the strongest Burton Ales; Bass No. 1 was first called a barley wine in 1872.

notes.aroma: Very rich bread, toffee and caramel malt with dried fruit and floral, earthy or marmalade hops.
notes.flavor: Layered malty sweetness and dark-fruit esters with soft alcohol; bitterness varies but malt leads.
notes.mouthfeel: Full, chewy and velvety with smooth warmth; low to moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like sipping beers with the richness of fruitcake or a good port

children.name: American Barleywine
children.description: Very strong, hoppy, bitter barleywine with caramel/toffee malt matched by citrusy, piney American hops.

parents.note: BJCP: an adaptation of the English style using American ingredients and balance.

notes.aroma: Strong malt richness with assertive citrusy, resiny American hops and warming alcohol.
notes.flavor: Rich bready, light-caramel malt against aggressive bitterness and big hop flavor; malty but always bitter.
notes.mouthfeel: Full, chewy and velvety with noticeable alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a big, slow-sipping beer that is both rich and seriously hoppy

children.name: Wheatwine
children.description: Barleywine-strength ale with 50%+ wheat: bready, honeyed, fruity malt, softer texture and moderate hops; may be oak-aged.
hops: Any; often American (Cascade, Centennial) or noble

parents.note: BJCP: more than simply a wheat-based barleywine, but built to barleywine strength as a winter or vintage release.
BJCP: wheatwine has its roots in American Wheat Beer rather than any German wheat style.

notes.aroma: Bready, wheaty malt with honey and caramel, light fruit and a clean alcohol note.
notes.flavor: Bready wheat malt leads, with honey, caramel and dried fruit; modest bitterness, never syrupy.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full, sleek and velvety; low to moderate carbonation, gentle warmth.

children.tryIf: you like barleywine but want something softer, breadier and less bitter

children.name: American Strong Ale
children.description: Strong, full-flavoured, hop-forward ale with caramel malt and assertive bitterness; spans 'double red' and 'imperial amber' ales.

parents.note: BJCP: modern versions were developed as 'imperial' strength American amber/red ales (Double Reds).

notes.aroma: Caramel and toffee malt with bold citrus, pine and resin hops and some alcohol.
notes.flavor: Strong caramel malt and high bitterness in balance, with big hop flavor and a bittersweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full body, warming, medium-low to medium carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like big, malty, aggressively hopped ales like Arrogant Bastard

children.name: Belgian & French Ales
children.description: Yeast-driven ales from Belgium and northern France: fruity esters, peppery phenols, high carbonation, often dry finishes and candi-sugar strength.

children.name: Abbey & Trappist Ales
children.description: Monastic-tradition ales built on Pilsner malt, candi sugar and expressive abbey yeast, from the light Single to the strong dark Quadrupel.

children.name: Trappist Single (Patersbier)
children.description: The monks' everyday table beer: pale, dry, hop-forward for a Belgian, with spicy-fruity yeast and a crisp, bitter finish.
children.yeast: Trappist/abbey ale yeast (e.g. Westmalle strain, WLP530/Wyeast 3787)

notes.aroma: Fruity-spicy Belgian yeast (pear, citrus, pepper) with floral, spicy hops and light honeyed malt.
notes.flavor: Soft cracker-and-honey malt, fruity-spicy yeast and spicy hops into a crisp, bitter, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, high and slightly prickly carbonation; no alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a light, dry, characterful Belgian beer for everyday drinking

children.name: Belgian Dubbel
children.description: Deep amber to copper, malty-rich ale with dark-fruit (raisin, plum) esters, caramelized-sugar depth and a fairly dry finish.
children.yearLabel: 1856 (Westmalle's first strong brown beer); modern recipe 1920s (BJCP gives 1922; Westmalle dates today's Dubbel to 1926)

notes.aroma: Rich malt with caramelized sugar and toast, raisin and plum esters and a touch of pepper.
notes.flavor: Malty-rich with dark fruit, caramel and gentle spice; low bitterness and a fairly dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Smooth, medium to medium-full body, lively carbonation, little alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like raisins, dried plums and caramel and want a complex but approachable abbey beer

adjuncts: Pale/white candi or table sugar (up to ~20%)
children.name: Belgian Tripel
children.description: Strong, pale gold, highly attenuated ale: spicy-fruity yeast (pepper, orange, banana), soft Pils malt, hidden alcohol and a dry, bitter finish.
children.yearLabel: early 1930s (BJCP: Westmalle, 1931; Witkap Pater c.1932; Westmalle 'Superbier' 1934, named Tripel 1956)

notes.aroma: Peppery, clove-like spice and orange-lemon esters over light honeyed malt, with soft alcohol.
notes.flavor: Spicy, fruity yeast, soft grainy-sweet malt and firm bitterness, ending dry rather than sweet.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, highly carbonated and effervescent; the strength is well hidden.

children.tryIf: you like strong golden beers that are spicy, fruity and surprisingly dry, like Westmalle Tripel

children.name: Belgian Dark Strong Ale
children.description: Rich, strong dark ale with caramel, toffee, dark fruit and spice, warming but dangerously drinkable thanks to high attenuation.

topSellers.name: Rochefort 10
topSellers.brewery: Brasserie de Rochefort (Abbaye Notre-Dame de Saint-Rémy)

children.name: Quadrupel (Quad)
children.description: The strongest end of the abbey range: amber to dark brown, plush body, figs, raisins, dark sugar and warming alcohol. BJCP folds it into 26D Belgian Dark Strong Ale; the Brewers Association lists Belgian-Style Quadrupel on its own (stats here are BA 2026).

parents.note: BJCP: 'Quad' is the name used, mainly outside Belgium, for Belgian Dark Strong Ale; Quadrupel itself is La Trappe's 1991 beer.

notes.aroma: Intense caramel and dark sugar with raisin, date, fig and plum, a little clove and evident alcohol.
notes.flavor: Rich caramel and dark-sugar malt with vinous dark fruit and strong but balanced alcohol.
notes.mouthfeel: Full and creamy under a dense, mousse-like head, with clear alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want the richest, strongest Belgian sipper, like St. Bernardus Abt 12

notes.aroma: Bready, dark-caramel malt with raisin, fig, plum and dried cherry, peppery spice and soft alcohol.
notes.flavor: Deep malt and dark fruit with gentle spice; moderately dry finish, with alcohol helping the balance.
notes.mouthfeel: Usually medium body (sometimes fuller and creamy), high carbonation, smooth warmth.

children.tryIf: you like complex, strong, dark-fruit beers like Chimay Blue or Rochefort 10

children.name: Pale & Golden Ales
children.description: Secular Belgian ales from the session-strength amber Spéciale Belge to the blond and devilishly strong golden ales.

children.name: Belgian Pale Ale (Spéciale Belge)
children.description: Amber to copper, moderate-strength, drinkable ale with toasty-biscuity malt, gentle fruity esters, low phenols and moderate bitterness.
children.yeast: Fruity Belgian ale yeast with low phenols (De Koninck-type)

topSellers.name: Palm Spéciale Belge
topSellers.brewery: Palm Belgian Craft Brewers (Swinkels Family Brewers)

parents.note: BJCP: created after a 1904 competition for a regional specialty to compete with imported British ales and continental lagers.

notes.aroma: Bready, toasty, biscuity malt with pear, orange and apple fruit and light spicy hops.
notes.flavor: Soft, smooth malt and moderate fruit, with supportive bitterness arriving late; balanced and dryish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth, medium to medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want an easy, balanced Belgian ale without heavy spice or strength, like De Koninck

children.name: Belgian Blond Ale
children.description: Golden, moderately strong, smooth and slightly sweet Pils-malt ale with light honeyed malt, soft fruity esters and a dry finish.

notes.aroma: Grainy-sweet, crackery malt with orange-lemon esters, light peppery spice and a hint of honey.
notes.flavor: Smooth, lightly sweet malt first, then citrusy yeast and light spice; soft, medium-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, lively mouth-filling carbonation, gentle warmth, sometimes creamy.

children.tryIf: you like golden, smooth, lightly fruity-spicy beers such as Leffe Blonde

children.name: Belgian Golden Strong Ale
children.description: Pale, very dry, highly carbonated and deceptively strong: pear and citrus esters, peppery phenols, spicy hops and a crisp, effervescent finish.
children.yeast: Fruity Belgian ale yeast (Duvel/Moortgat strain, WLP570)
children.yearLabel: by the 1970s (pale form, BJCP); Moortgat's darker original brewed from after WWI, named Duvel 1923

notes.aroma: Pear and apple esters, herbal or spicy hops and peppery alcohol over a nearly neutral malt base.
notes.flavor: Pear-like fruit, peppery spice and herbal hops on soft malt; firm bitterness and a long, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body, very high, Champagne-like carbonation; deceptive alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like Duvel: pale, sparkling, fruity and dangerously drinkable for its strength

children.name: Belgian White
children.description: Spiced, hazy wheat ales from the Brabant countryside around Hoegaarden.

children.name: Witbier
children.description: Hazy, pale, refreshing wheat ale with coriander and orange-peel spice, a light lactic-citrus tartness and a creamy, effervescent body.
children.yearLabel: c.1500 (medieval Leuven/Hoegaarden white beers; date approx.); died out 1957, revived 1966 by Pierre Celis

notes.aroma: Orange peel and lemony coriander over bready wheat, with light honey and peppery spice.
notes.flavor: Bready wheat with zesty orange, subtle spice and low bitterness; crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth and lightly creamy, with high, fizzy carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like hazy, citrusy, lightly spiced and refreshing wheat beers like Hoegaarden

children.name: Farmhouse Ales
children.description: Rustic, dry ales of Wallonia and French Flanders, historically brewed on farms for seasonal workers.

children.name: Saison
children.description: Dry, highly carbonated, fruity-spicy pale ale with peppery yeast, firm bitterness and a refreshing, bone-dry finish. BJCP recognises table (3.5–5%), standard (5–7%) and super (7–9.5%) strengths and pale (5–14 SRM) or dark (15–22 SRM) versions; the stats here are for standard pale.
children.yeast: Highly attenuative, peppery saison yeast (Dupont strain, WLP565/Wyeast 3724)

children.name: Super Saison
children.description: The strong end of BJCP 25B: same dry, peppery, fruity profile with more alcohol warmth and fuller malt.

topSellers.name: Saison Dupont Avec Les Bons Voeux

children.yearLabel: 1954 (Dupont's first 'super saison', per BJCP); US craft strong saisons 1990s–2000s

parents.note: BJCP: Dupont's stronger 'super saison' was first produced in 1954; strength variants of saison.

notes.aroma: Intense fruity-peppery yeast and spicy hops with more malt and a light, clean alcohol note.
notes.flavor: Fruit and pepper over a firmer malt base, warming alcohol and firm bitterness; still finishes dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, very high carbonation, some warmth.

children.tryIf: you like saison and want a stronger, richer version that still finishes dry

children.yearLabel: by the 1800s (Wallonian farmhouse provision ale; date approx.); Saison Dupont 1920s

notes.aroma: Peppery yeast spice with citrus, pear or stone-fruit esters and spicy, earthy continental hops.
notes.flavor: Fruity, peppery yeast, grainy malt and firm hop bitterness; very dry, bitter-spicy finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-low body with very high, effervescent carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want a dry, spicy, refreshing farmhouse ale (Saison Dupont is the benchmark)

children.name: Grisette
children.description: Light, low-alcohol wheat-inclusive farmhouse ale, historically for Hainaut quarry and mine workers: crisp, dry, lemony and gently hopped. Not in BJCP or the BA 2026 guidelines; stats follow the BYO style profile, and modern commercial versions often run stronger (about 4-5.5%).

parents.note: BJCP: a well-known type of Saison popular with miners (session-strength, with wheat).

notes.aroma: Light wheat and grainy malt with peppery farmhouse yeast and floral, spicy or citrus hops.
notes.flavor: Crisp and lean with gentle yeast spice, light fruit and firm hop bitterness; very dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body with high carbonation; spritzy and thirst-quenching.

children.tryIf: you want a low-alcohol, dry, hoppy farmhouse beer for warm days

children.name: Bière de Garde
children.description: Malt-focused, cellar-aged French farmhouse ale in blonde, ambrée or brune versions: toasty, lightly caramel, clean and smooth with a dry finish.
children.yeast: Clean ale or lager yeast fermented cool, then long cold conditioning

notes.aroma: Toasty, bready, biscuity malt richness with low fruit and a whisper of spicy hops.
notes.flavor: Malty, with toast, toffee and light caramel, low bitterness and a smooth, medium-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body, smooth and silky, moderate to high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like malty amber beers and want something smooth, rich and dry

children.name: Wheat Beers
children.description: Beers with a large share of malted wheat (or rye), from Bavarian banana-and-clove Weissbier to clean American wheat ales.

children.name: German Weissbier
children.description: Bavarian top-fermented wheat beers with at least 50% wheat malt and a weizen yeast giving banana esters and clove phenols.

children.name: Weissbier (Hefeweizen)
children.description: Pale, hazy, highly carbonated wheat beer with banana and clove from weizen yeast, soft bready wheat and a light, fluffy body.
children.yeast: Bavarian weizen yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan 68 / WLP300 / Wyeast 3068)

children.name: Kristallweizen
children.description: Filtered, brilliantly clear Weissbier: the same banana-clove yeast character, a bit crisper and lighter without the yeast. The BA lists South German-Style Kristal Weizen separately (straw to amber, stats here are BA 2026); BJCP includes filtered versions under 10A.
children.yeast: Bavarian weizen yeast, filtered before packaging

parents.note: Filtered version of Bavarian Weissbier; BJCP still treats filtered examples within 10A Weissbier.

notes.aroma: Banana and clove like a Hefeweizen, but cleaner and brighter without the yeasty bread note.
notes.flavor: Clove and banana over light wheat; crisp and dry with very low bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Lighter and cleaner than an unfiltered Weissbier; very highly carbonated and spritzy.

children.tryIf: you like Hefeweizen flavors but want a cleaner, sparkling, brilliantly clear glass

children.name: Leichtes Weizen
children.description: Reduced-alcohol, lower-calorie Weissbier: lighter body with the same banana-clove yeast character in a softer form.

parents.note: Reduced-alcohol, lower-calorie version of Weissbier brewed by the big Bavarian wheat-beer brewers.

notes.aroma: Gentle banana and clove with a light wheat-bread note; softer than full-strength Weissbier.
notes.flavor: Mild banana-clove over thin wheat malt; low bitterness, simple and quenching.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body and watery-to-soft texture; high carbonation keeps it lively.

children.tryIf: you want Weissbier flavor at low alcohol for a hot day or a long session

children.yearLabel: 16th century (Bavarian ducal wheat-beer privilege); modern Weissbier 1872 (Schneider); pale form popular from 1960s

notes.aroma: Banana and clove up front over soft bread dough and wheat; hops barely there.
notes.flavor: Banana-clove yeast over bready wheat; very low bitterness and a fairly dry, refreshing finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium, fluffy and creamy; very lively carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like banana bread, clove and soft, refreshing beers with almost no bitterness

children.name: Dunkles Weissbier
children.description: Dark Weissbier: banana-clove yeast over bready, toasty Munich and dark wheat malt with hints of caramel; light, creamy and refreshing.

origin.era: Traditional; older than pale Weissbier in common use

children.yearLabel: traditional dark Bavarian wheat beer; modern form from 1872 (Schneider)

parents.note: BJCP: old-fashioned Bavarian wheat beer was often dark, and the dark form survived after pale Weissbier became popular in the 1960s.

notes.aroma: Banana and clove woven with bread crust, caramel and toasted wheat.
notes.flavor: Toasty, bready malt and a hint of caramel meet banana-clove yeast; low bitterness, fairly dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium-full, creamy and fluffy; effervescent.

children.tryIf: you like Hefeweizen but want more toasted-bread and caramel depth

children.name: Weizenbock
children.description: Strong pale or dark wheat bock: rich bready/caramel malt, dark-fruit or banana esters, clove and warming alcohol. A freeze-concentrated 'Weizen-Eisbock' version exists (Schneider Aventinus Eisbock, ~12%), but it has no separate guideline.

parents.note: A Weissbier brewed to bock or doppelbock strength, created at Schneider Weisse in Munich.
BJCP: Aventinus was created in 1907 at Schneider as a doppelbock-strength wheat beer.

notes.aroma: Rich bready wheat malt with banana, clove and, in dark versions, plum, raisin and light alcohol.
notes.flavor: Malty and rich with banana-spice yeast and dark fruit; low bitterness, slightly sweet but finishing dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full, soft and creamy; mild alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you love banana-clove wheat beer and want it big, malty and warming like a bock

children.name: Roggenbier
children.description: German rye beer brewed like a Dunkelweizen: grainy, spicy rye with banana-clove weizen yeast, a thick, creamy body and moderate brown color.

origin.era: Medieval rye beers; modern style 1988 (Schierlinger Roggen, later Thurn und Taxis / Paulaner)

parents.note: Essentially a Dunkles Weissbier brewed with malted rye instead of wheat, using weizen yeast.

notes.aroma: Peppery rye bread and pumpernickel with clove and banana or citrus esters.
notes.flavor: Spicy, grainy rye over a hint of caramel, with weizen yeast character and a lightly bitter, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full and creamy; high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like rye bread and Dunkelweizen and want a spicier, fuller version

children.name: American Wheat
children.description: Wheat beers fermented with clean ale or lager yeast, so no banana or clove.

adjuncts: Fruit or citrus in some versions
children.name: American Wheat Beer
children.description: Pale, refreshing wheat ale with clean fermentation, soft bready wheat and light-to-moderate American or noble hop character.
children.yeast: Clean American ale yeast (e.g. Chico/US-05) or lager yeast; no weizen yeast

parents.note: American craft adaptation of Weissbier with a cleaner yeast and more hops.

notes.aroma: Light bread dough and wheat with a touch of citrus, floral or spicy hops; no banana or clove.
notes.flavor: Clean wheat-bread flavor with low to moderate hops; even balance and a crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light, soft and highly carbonated.

children.tryIf: you want an easy, clean wheat beer without the banana-clove yeast

children.name: Wild & Sour
children.description: Beers made sour or funky by Lactobacillus, Pediococcus, Brettanomyces or spontaneous fermentation, from Berliner Weisse to aged lambic.

children.name: German Sour Wheat
children.description: Light, tart wheat beers from northern and eastern Germany, soured with lactic acid bacteria.

children.name: Berliner Weisse
children.description: Very pale, low-alcohol, sharply sour and highly carbonated wheat beer: clean lactic tartness, bready wheat and a dry finish. Often served 'mit Schuss' with raspberry or woodruff syrup.
children.yeast: Top-fermenting ale yeast co-fermented with Lactobacillus (sometimes Brett)

topSellers.name: Berliner Kindl Weisse
topSellers.brewery: Berliner Kindl Schultheiss (Radeberger Gruppe / Oetker Group)

children.yearLabel: 16th–17th century (earliest Berlin record often given as 1572); "Champagne of the North" by 1809

notes.aroma: Sharp lactic tang with sourdough and light lemon, tart apple or apricot notes.
notes.flavor: Clean, bright sourness over raw bread dough; no hop bitterness and a bone-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light but not thin; very high carbonation and crisp acidity.

children.tryIf: you like tart lemonade and sourdough and want a very low-alcohol thirst quencher

children.name: Gose
children.description: Tart, lightly salty wheat beer with bright coriander-lemon spice, low bitterness and a refreshing, highly carbonated finish.
children.yeast: Clean ale yeast with Lactobacillus (kettle- or co-souring)

topSellers.name: Anderson Valley The Kimmie, The Yink & The Holy Gose

children.yearLabel: medieval (Goslar); in Leipzig by 1740; extinct 1966, revived 1980s

notes.aroma: Lemony coriander, light sourdough and a faint sea-breeze saltiness.
notes.flavor: Moderate tartness, bready wheat and a hint of salt and coriander; dry and refreshing.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium, effervescent; salt can feel round and mouthwatering.

children.tryIf: you like salty-sour flavors such as margaritas, pickles or citrus with sea salt

children.name: Flemish Sour Ales
children.description: West and East Flanders' aged, acetic-to-lactic sour ales with malt and fruit complexity.

children.name: Flanders Red Ale
children.description: Burgundy-red, wine-like sour ale: cherry, plum and red-currant fruit, lactic and gentle acetic sourness, oak and a balancing malt sweetness.
children.yeast: Ale yeast plus Lactobacillus, Pediococcus, Brettanomyces and acetic bacteria; long oak foeder aging
children.yearLabel: 1821 (Rodenbach brewery founded); oak-vat aged red-brown style from the 1870s

parents.note: Eugène Rodenbach began ageing the brewery's beer in large oak vats in the 1870s after brewing London porter in England; BJCP says the vat ageing and blending were borrowed from the English tradition.

notes.aroma: Black cherry, plum, red currant and orange over toasty malt with a vinegary-wine edge.
notes.flavor: Fruity, complex sourness with light acetic bite and soft malt; tannic, wine-like finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body with tannin and a prickly acidity; low to medium carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like red wine, balsamic and sour cherries

children.name: Oud Bruin
children.description: Malty, brown East Flanders sour: caramel, toffee and dark fruit with a soft lactic (not acetic) tartness; aged in steel rather than oak.
children.yeast: Ale yeast with Lactobacillus (and Sacch); aged

notes.aroma: Caramel, toffee and dark fruit like raisin, plum and fig, with a gentle sour note.
notes.flavor: Malty sweet-and-sour: dark fruit and caramel with mild lactic tartness, sometimes sherry-like.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, smooth; low to moderate carbonation and some warmth when strong.

children.tryIf: you like dried fruit and caramel and want a soft, sweet-and-sour brown beer

children.name: Lambic Family
children.description: Spontaneously fermented wheat beers of the Senne valley and Pajottenland around Brussels, aged in oak and blended.

children.name: Lambic
children.description: Unblended, often still, spontaneously fermented wheat beer: sour, funky (barnyard, hay, horse blanket), with lemony and oak notes and almost no hop bitterness.
hops: Aged (3+ years) low-alpha hops, used as preservative
children.yeast: Spontaneous fermentation (coolship): Sacch, Brettanomyces, Lactobacillus, Pediococcus and others
children.yearLabel: at least 16th century (Senne valley farmhouse tradition)

notes.aroma: Sour with barnyard, hay and earthy funk, plus lemon, apple or rhubarb notes.
notes.flavor: Strong lactic sourness and wild funk over faint grainy wheat; no bitterness, very dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light; usually flat or nearly still with a puckering tartness.

children.tryIf: you like sour, funky natural wine or farmhouse cider

children.name: Gueuze
children.description: Blend of 1-, 2- and 3-year-old lambics refermented in the bottle: sparkling, intensely sour and complex with funk, citrus, oak and a bone-dry finish. Sweetened commercial gueuzes (Belle-Vue, Mort Subite) outsell the traditional 'oude' versions.
children.yeast: Spontaneous mixed fermentation; bottle refermentation from young lambic
children.yearLabel: 1830s–40s first bottled gueuze; blended champagne-bottle form later 1800s

parents.note: Blend of young and old lambic, bottle-conditioned; same basic history as lambic.

notes.aroma: Complex funk (barnyard, leather, hay) with citrus, apple and a light oak and honey note.
notes.flavor: Sour and funky with citrus fruit, oak and a crisp, bone-dry tart finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light and highly carbonated, almost champagne-like.

children.tryIf: you like Champagne, sour cider or funky natural wine

children.name: Faro
children.description: Lambic sweetened with brown or candi sugar (historically blended with weaker beer): sweet-sour, caramel and light funk. BJCP only mentions it in the 23D Lambic comments and gives no separate stats; ranges here are the 23D numbers widened to cover commercial versions (about 4-5%).
children.yeast: Spontaneous fermentation (lambic base); modern bottled versions pasteurised

parents.note: Brussels café beer: lambic blended with weaker meerts and sweetened with sugar.

notes.aroma: Light funk and tartness softened by brown sugar and caramel.
notes.flavor: Sweet-and-sour: lambic acidity balanced by candi or brown sugar, with mild funk.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light; often low carbonation and a soft, rounded feel.

children.tryIf: you are curious about lambic but prefer something sweeter and gentler

adjuncts: Whole fruit: peach, apricot, blackcurrant, grape and others
children.name: Fruit Lambic
children.description: Lambic or gueuze refermented on whole fruit: the fruit leads, over a sour, funky, dry lambic base. Modern mass-market versions are sweetened and pasteurised.

children.name: Kriek
children.description: Cherry lambic, traditionally made with sour Schaerbeek cherries: tart cherry and almond-like pit over a funky, dry lambic base. BJCP 23F color (3-7 SRM) varies with the fruit, so real examples are often deep red.
children.yearLabel: 19th-century tradition; documented recipes by c. 1900 (Schaerbeek cherries)

parents.note: Sour Schaerbeek cherries macerated in lambic, traditionally by the blender or publican.

notes.aroma: Tart sour cherry with almond-like cherry pit over earthy lambic funk.
notes.flavor: Sour cherry and funk with a dry, tart finish; sweetened versions taste like cherry soda.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light, lively carbonation and a puckering acidity.

children.tryIf: you love sour cherries, cherry pie or Amarena cherries

children.name: Framboise
children.description: Raspberry lambic: vivid raspberry aroma and pink-red color with sour, funky lambic character. BJCP 23F color (3-7 SRM) varies with the fruit, so real examples are often deep red.

parents.note: Raspberries macerated in lambic, following the fruit-lambic tradition.

notes.aroma: Intense fresh raspberry over light funk and tartness.
notes.flavor: Bright raspberry and sharp acidity; traditional versions dry, popular commercial ones noticeably sweet.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light and spritzy; tart and refreshing.

children.tryIf: you like raspberries, raspberry sorbet or fruity rosé

children.yearLabel: c. 1900 (kriek first); other fruits 20th century; sweetened versions from 1970s

parents.note: Fruit added to lambic by blenders and publicans to vary café offerings.
BJCP: "same basic history as Gueuze", with fruit (and in modern versions sugar) added to the blend.

notes.aroma: Vivid fermented fruit over gueuze-like funk, citrus and earthy notes; fruit varies.
notes.flavor: Fruit leads over sour, funky lambic; traditional versions dry, sweetened commercial ones fruit-juicy.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light; sparkling to nearly still with a tart pucker.

children.tryIf: you like tart fruit, fruit wine or sour candy

children.name: American Wild & Mixed Fermentation
children.description: Modern wild ales, mostly American, using Brett, Lacto, Pedio or house mixed cultures, often barrel-aged and fruited. BJCP gives no fixed vital statistics; they vary with the base beer.

children.name: American Wild Ale
children.description: Umbrella for American-made sour and funky ales: any base beer fermented or aged with wild yeast and/or bacteria, often in oak, with fruit, funk and acidity in any balance. BJCP gives no vital statistics (variable by base style); the ranges shown are deliberately broad.
malts: Specialty malts as for base style
hops: Low-alpha or aged hops (hops inhibit Lacto)
children.yeast: House mixed cultures: Sacch with Brett, Lactobacillus and/or Pediococcus; coolship spontaneous in some

children.name: Brett Beer
children.description: Any base beer fermented or finished with Brettanomyces but no bacteria: tropical, stone-fruit or barnyard funk, very dry, not intentionally sour. BJCP gives no vital statistics (variable by base style); the ranges shown are deliberately broad.
children.yeast: Brettanomyces (100% Brett or Sacch primary + Brett); no Lacto/Pedio

parents.note: American wild-ale subtype fermented with Brettanomyces, inspired by Belgian wild ales and historical Brett-aged English beers.

notes.aroma: Tropical, stone-fruit or pineapple notes from Brett, with a little barnyard funk as it ages.
notes.flavor: Dry and fruity over the base beer; earthy funk but not sour (at most a light tang).
notes.mouthfeel: Lighter than the base style; dry, crisp and well carbonated.

children.tryIf: you like farmhouse funk and fruity, bone-dry beers but not sourness

children.name: Mixed-Fermentation Sour Beer
children.description: Sour, funky beer from any combination of Sacch, Brett, Lacto and Pedio, often oak-aged: layered acidity, fruity esters and Brett complexity. BJCP gives no vital statistics (variable by base style); the ranges shown are deliberately broad.
children.yeast: Mixed culture: Sacch + Brettanomyces + Lactobacillus + Pediococcus

parents.note: Subcategory of American wild ale using mixed Sacch/Brett/bacteria cultures.
Modern American interpretations of Belgian sour ales.
Modern American interpretations of Belgian sour ales.

notes.aroma: Layered acidity with fruity esters, funk and often oak; varies with base beer.
notes.flavor: Firm, complex sourness and Brett character; low bitterness, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Lighter than the base beer; moderate to high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like Flanders reds and gueuze and want American takes on sour and funky

children.name: Wild Specialty Beer
children.description: A Brett, mixed-fermentation or sour beer with fruit, herbs, spices or distinctive wood/barrel character (e.g. wine or spirit barrels). BJCP gives no vital statistics (variable by base style); the ranges shown are deliberately broad.

parents.note: American wild ale with fruit, spice, wood or other specialty additions.
Fruited wild ales are interpretations of fruited Belgian wild ales.

notes.aroma: Wild funk and acidity blended with fruit, spices or wine and spirit barrel notes; varies widely.
notes.flavor: Tart, funky and dry with the added fruit or wood clearly present; balance depends on the beer.
notes.mouthfeel: Generally light to medium; fruit or wood tannins can add grip.

children.tryIf: you like fruited sours and barrel-aged wild beers

children.yearLabel: late 1990s–2000s (New Belgium, Russian River, Jolly Pumpkin)

parents.note: Modern American interpretations of, or experiments inspired by, Belgian wild ales.
Barrel-aged sour reds/browns such as New Belgium La Folie follow the Flemish sour model.

notes.aroma: Fruity and funky: stone fruit, citrus or tropical notes with barnyard and oak; varies widely.
notes.flavor: Usually tart and dry with fruity esters and Brett funk; base beer and acidity vary a lot.
notes.mouthfeel: Generally light to medium, dry and moderately to highly carbonated.

children.tryIf: you like experimenting with sour, funky, barrel-aged beers

children.name: Kettle & Fruited Sours
children.description: Fast, clean lactic sours (kettle-soured or co-fermented), usually loaded with fruit, from the US craft scene and Brazil.

adjuncts: Fruit puree (passion fruit, raspberry, mango, guava)
children.name: Fruited Kettle Sour
children.description: Clean, bright lactic sour (no Brett funk) on a pale or wheat base, heavily fruited; color and flavor follow the fruit. The BA lists it as American-Style Fruited Sour Ale but says all stats "may vary widely"; ABV/IBU here follow the unfruited base, BJCP 28D Straight Sour Beer, with a broad color range for the fruit.
children.yeast: Kettle souring with Lactobacillus, then clean ale yeast (or lactic-producing yeast such as Philly Sour)

parents.note: BJCP: kettle souring is the Francke acidification process developed to speed up traditional Berliner Weisse production.
BJCP notes Gose is often used as a base for fruited sour beers.

notes.aroma: Loud fruit (passion fruit, raspberry, mango and so on) over clean lactic tartness.
notes.flavor: Fruit-forward and tart with no funk or bitterness; sweetness varies and some are smoothie-thick.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium; spritzy, though heavily fruited versions feel fuller.

children.tryIf: you like sour candy, fruit juice and tart fruit desserts

adjuncts: Fresh fruit (araçá, jabuticaba, peach, passion fruit, guava, tangerine)
children.name: Catharina Sour
children.description: Brazilian light, refreshing wheat-based kettle sour with fresh (often tropical) fruit: clean lactic tartness, no perceptible bitterness, no Brett, fruit-forward and dry. BJCP 2021 Appendix B local style X4.
children.yeast: Kettle souring with Lactobacillus, then clean ale yeast

topSellers.name: Blumenau Catharina Sour Sun of a Peach (Pêssego)

parents.note: BJCP: like a stronger Berliner Weisse, but with fresh fruit and no Brett.
BJCP: a fruited sour wheat beer, most commonly kettle-soured with Lacto and fruited late, formally defined in Santa Catarina, Brazil, in 2015.

notes.aroma: Fresh, often tropical fruit with a clean lactic tang; no hop aroma or funk.
notes.flavor: Fresh fruit dominates over light wheat, with a clean tartness and a dry finish; no bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Low to medium-low body; highly carbonated and very refreshing.

children.tryIf: you want a light, fresh-fruit sour that is tart but not punishing

children.name: Grape Ales
children.description: Beer-wine hybrids fermented with grape must. Placed here because many Italian Grape Ales show light tartness or wild character; the international 29D Grape Ale sits with fruit beers in the Specialty family.

adjuncts: Grape must or sapa (cooked must), red or white varieties
children.name: Italian Grape Ale
children.description: Italian ale fermented with grape must or grapes (up to ~40% of the grist): vinous grape and fruit aromas, often light tartness or a low wild character, dry and highly carbonated. BJCP 2021 Appendix B local style X3 (stats here); non-Italian versions go in 29D Grape Ale, which has narrower stats (6-8.5% ABV, 4-8 SRM).
hops: Low-alpha Old World hops (German or English), used sparingly
children.yeast: Neutral ale yeast (most common) or fruity/spicy Belgian/English strains; some with wild yeast or wine yeast

notes.aroma: Grape must and wine-like fruit (stone fruit for white grapes, red fruit for red) over light malt.
notes.flavor: Vinous grape flavor with gentle tartness, restrained malt and low bitterness; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium, highly carbonated, sparkling-wine-like.

children.tryIf: you like sparkling wine or are a wine drinker curious about beer

children.name: Lagers
children.description: Bottom-fermented beers that are cold-fermented and cold-conditioned (lagered), giving a clean, crisp profile. They range from ice-cold light lagers to strong Bavarian bocks.

children.name: Light & International Pale Lagers
children.description: Mass-market pale lagers: very pale, highly carbonated, low bitterness, often brewed with rice or corn.

children.name: American Light Lager
children.description: Very pale, very light-bodied, highly carbonated lager with minimal malt and hop flavor and a crisp, dry finish; built to be served ice cold. Michelob Ultra became the No. 1 US beer by volume in 2025 (Circana, 52 weeks to Sept. 2025), overtaking Modelo Especial; Bud Light lost the top spot in 2023.
children.yeast: Clean American lager yeast; added enzymes for very high attenuation

parents.note: Diet-conscious, lower-calorie version of the standard American lager.

notes.aroma: Very faint grain or corn and barely any hops; clean.
notes.flavor: Nearly neutral with a hint of grainy sweetness and very low bitterness; crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Very light, almost watery; very high carbonation with a slight carbonic bite.

children.tryIf: you want something ice cold, light and easy with almost no flavor to think about

children.name: American Lager
children.description: Very pale, highly carbonated, crisp and clean adjunct lager with a neutral grainy palate and low bitterness; slightly fuller than light lager.
children.yearLabel: post-1933 (after Prohibition and WWII, BJCP); roots in 1870s adjunct lagers such as Budweiser (1876)

parents.note: Evolved from Pre-Prohibition Lager after Prohibition and WWII as surviving breweries consolidated.

notes.aroma: Light grain or corn and a faint spicy-floral hop note; clean.
notes.flavor: Neutral grainy-corn flavor with low bitterness and a crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body; very highly carbonated.
