children.tryIf: you like a cold, crisp, familiar lager for barbecues and ballgames

children.name: International Pale Lager
children.description: Highly attenuated pale lager with a little more body and hop bitterness than American lager; the worldwide mass-market "premium lager".
children.yearLabel: by the mid-20th century (mass-market premium lagers; date approx.)

parents.note: BJCP: developed in the US as a premium version of standard American lager and abroad as an imitation of American-style lagers.
BJCP: outside the US also developed as a more accessible, drier and less bitter version of Pilsner-type beer.

notes.aroma: Grainy malt with light corn sweetness and a low spicy or floral hop note.
notes.flavor: Clean grainy malt, medium-low bitterness and a crisp, well-attenuated finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body; lively carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like mainstream imported lagers with a bit more bite than US lagers

children.name: Mexican Lager
children.description: Clean, crisp, very pale lager with a light grainy-corn sweetness and low hop character; often served with lime. The Brewers Association lists Mexican-Style Light, Pale, Amber and Dark Lager separately; stats shown are BA Mexican-Style Pale Lager. BJCP has no separate style (Corona Extra is a BJCP 2A example).

topSellers.name: Corona Extra
topSellers.brewery: Grupo Modelo (AB InBev; Constellation Brands in US)

topSellers.name: Modelo Especial
topSellers.brewery: Grupo Modelo (AB InBev; Constellation Brands in US)

topSellers.name: Pacifico
topSellers.brewery: Grupo Modelo (AB InBev; Constellation Brands in US)

parents.note: BJCP: Vienna lager was brought to Mexico by Santiago Graf and other Austrian immigrant brewers in the late 1800s, founding Mexican lager brewing.

notes.aroma: Light grain and corn sweetness with a faint noble-hop note.
notes.flavor: Clean, crisp and lightly grainy with low bitterness and a dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body; bright carbonation; great with a lime wedge.

children.tryIf: you want a beach beer to drink cold with tacos and lime

children.name: Rice Lager
children.description: Very pale, brilliantly clear, dry ("karakuchi") lager in which rice (at least 15% of the grist under BA rules) lightens the body and sharpens the finish; hops stay integrated rather than dominant. Stats are the BA "Rice Lager" guideline; BJCP has no separate style (Asahi Super Dry is a BJCP 2A example).

origin.era: Rice in lagers since 1800s; Asahi Super Dry 1987

children.yearLabel: rice adjunct lagers since late 1800s; dry style 1987 (Asahi Super Dry)

parents.note: Asahi Super Dry (1987) was a drier reformulation of mass-market pale lager, and BJCP lists it as a 2A International Pale Lager.

notes.aroma: Very clean with faint grain and rice; hops subtle.
notes.flavor: Crisp, dry and neutral with a quick, sharp finish and moderate integrated bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body, highly carbonated and very clean; the driest of the pale lagers.

children.tryIf: you want the crispest, driest lager to go with sushi or fried food

children.name: American Malt Liquor
children.description: Strong, very pale, high-adjunct lager with a sweet corn-sugar character, minimal hops and noticeable alcohol warmth. BA notes that some are barely stronger than American lager while others approach bock strength; market leader Steel Reserve 211 (8.1%) sits above the BA 6.3-7.6% range.

parents.note: Stronger, high-adjunct variant of American mass-market lager.

notes.aroma: Sweet corn and grain with a whiff of alcohol and light fruitiness; no hops.
notes.flavor: Sweetish corn-sugar malt and noticeable alcohol with very little bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light body that belies its strength; some warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a strong, cheap, sweetish lager with no bitterness

children.name: German Pale Lagers
children.description: Malt-led pale lagers from Bavaria and northern Germany: soft grainy Pils malt and restrained noble hops.

children.name: Munich Helles
children.description: Clean, malty, gold lager with a smooth grainy-sweet Pils malt flavor, soft finish and just enough noble-hop bitterness for balance.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Created in Munich to compete with pale Pilsner-type beers.

notes.aroma: Grainy-sweet Pilsner malt with a gentle spicy-floral hop note.
notes.flavor: Soft, bready-grainy malt leads with just enough bitterness; smooth, soft dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, medium carbonation; very smooth.

children.tryIf: you like soft, bready, malty beer that is easy to drink by the liter

children.name: Festbier
children.description: Golden, smooth, rich-but-clean lager served at the Munich Oktoberfest since the 1970s; fuller than Helles with a bready Pils-malt depth.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Paulaner developed a lighter, golden, more drinkable version of the traditional Oktoberfest Märzen.

notes.aroma: Toasty bread dough and rich Pils malt with light floral hops.
notes.flavor: Rich, lightly toasty malt with supportive bitterness; clean and crisp but not dry.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, smooth and slightly creamy; strength well hidden.

children.tryIf: you like Helles but want a richer, stronger Oktoberfest-tent golden lager

children.name: German Helles Exportbier (Dortmunder Export)
children.description: Pale, well-balanced, smooth lager that is a bit stronger than Helles and bolder in body and bitterness, with a minerally dry finish from Dortmund water.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Developed in Dortmund in response to pale Pilsner-type beers.

notes.aroma: Grainy-sweet malt with light toast and a moderate floral-spicy hop note.
notes.flavor: Balanced malt and hops with medium bitterness and a minerally, medium-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, smooth and mellow.

children.tryIf: you want a golden lager that sits between Helles and Pils, a bit stronger and fuller

children.name: Kellerbier
children.description: Unfiltered, unpasteurized German lager traditionally served young from the lagering vessel; may be a Helles, Pils, Märzen or Dunkel base and is a little richer, more rustic and often slightly hazier than the filtered base style. BJCP and BA both give stats "same as / varies with base style"; the ranges shown are an approximate envelope spanning Pils/Helles to Märzen bases.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70); left unfiltered
children.yearLabel: 1800s (Franconian cellar lagers); now a broad term for unfiltered lager

notes.aroma: Fresh bread and yeast over the base lager; hoppier when pale, richer when dark. Varies with base.
notes.flavor: Like its base lager but more rustic: bready, a little more bitter and a touch fuller.
notes.mouthfeel: Slightly fuller and creamier than the filtered base; often softer carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like fresh, unfiltered beer straight from the tank

children.name: German Leichtbier
children.description: Pale, highly attenuated, light-bodied German lager with lower alcohol and calories than standard beers but still noticeable malt and noble-hop flavor.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Modern versions are based on popular American light lagers, aimed at health-conscious drinkers.

notes.aroma: Light grainy-cracker malt with spicy, herbal noble hops.
notes.flavor: Light malt, medium bitterness and noticeable hop flavor; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to very light body; medium to high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want a low-alcohol lager that still tastes like German hops and malt

children.name: Pilsners & Hoppy Pale Lagers
children.description: Hop-forward pale lagers descended from the 1842 Pilsen original, plus modern dry-hopped and New World versions.

children.name: German Pils
children.description: Light gold, crisp, dry and bitter lager with a flowery-spicy noble hop aroma and a clean grainy malt base.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Adapted from Czech Pilsner to harder German water and German hop varieties.

notes.aroma: Floral, spicy and herbal noble hops over light honey and cracker malt.
notes.flavor: Brief grainy malt then firm, lingering bitterness and hop flavor; crisp, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light; medium to high carbonation and sometimes a minerally sharpness.

children.tryIf: you like crisp, bitter, refreshing lagers with flowery hops

children.name: Czech Premium Pale Lager (Bohemian Pilsner)
children.description: Rich, complex golden lager with a bready Czech-malt depth, soft rounded Saaz bitterness, spicy hop aroma and often a touch of diacetyl.
children.yeast: Czech lager yeast (e.g. Pilsen H strain / WLP800)

parents.note: BJCP: Bavarian brewer Josef Groll brought Bavarian bottom-fermenting lager methods to Plzeň, where they were combined with English malting techniques.

notes.aroma: Rich bready malt and spicy-floral Saaz hops; sometimes a hint of butterscotch.
notes.flavor: Bready malt and soft, rounded but firm bitterness with a long finish; often a light diacetyl note.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body; moderate to low carbonation and a soft, rounded feel.

children.tryIf: you like malt-rich, bitter-but-smooth golden lager like Pilsner Urquell

children.name: Czech Pale Lager (Světlé výčepní)
children.description: Light, rich, refreshing and hoppy everyday Czech draft lager (about 10° Plato) with a bready malt flavor and soft Saaz bitterness.

parents.note: Groll brewed a smaller výčepní alongside the ležák in 1842–3; the lighter sibling of the original Pilsner.

notes.aroma: Light bready malt with spicy, herbal Saaz hops.
notes.flavor: Bready-rich malt, prominent but soft bitterness and a rounded hoppy finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium; moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want a light, hoppy, flavorful lager to drink several of

children.name: Italian Pilsner
children.description: A German-style Pils that is dry-hopped with noble hops, giving an intense floral-herbal aroma over a crisp, dry, pale base. Named after Birrificio Italiano Tipopils (1996). Stats are the BA "Italian-Style Pilsener" guideline; BJCP has no separate style (Tipopils is a 34B Mixed-Style example).
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Agostino Arioli, trained in German breweries, set out to brew a northern German-style Pils and dry-hopped it with noble hops.

notes.aroma: Intense floral, herbal and peppery noble-hop aroma from dry hopping over light malt.
notes.flavor: Crisp light malt, firm bitterness and bright fresh-hop flavor; very dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light; lively carbonation and a crisp feel.

children.tryIf: you like German Pils but want more fresh hop aroma

children.name: New Zealand Pilsner
children.description: Pale, dry, crisp lager-like beer showcasing New Zealand hops with tropical, white-wine and lime notes and a firm clean bitterness.
children.yeast: Clean lager yeast or very neutral ale yeast

parents.note: Emerson's described its Pilsner as a take on the Czech/German style, originally hopped with Saaz D (now Riwaka).
Emerson's described its Pilsner as a take on the Czech/German style, reinterpreted with New Zealand hops.

notes.aroma: Tropical fruit, lime, gooseberry and white-wine hops with a grassy edge over cracker malt.
notes.flavor: Clean bitterness and juicy-tropical hop flavor over bready malt; dry, smooth finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-light, soft and smooth; never harsh.

children.tryIf: you like Sauvignon Blanc and hoppy pale ales but want a crisp lager

children.name: India Pale Lager (IPL)
children.description: A crisp, clean lager hopped like an American IPA, with heavy late and dry hopping (citrus, tropical, pine) over a dry, lightly malty base. Stats are the BA "American-Style India Pale Lager" guideline; BJCP has no IPL style and sends these to 34B Mixed-Style (Hoponius Union is a 34B example). "Cold IPA" is a closely related offshoot.

parents.note: A pale lager hopped like an American IPA, fermented cold and lagered.

notes.aroma: Big citrus, tropical and pine hops over a clean, light malt base.
notes.flavor: Bold hop flavor and high bitterness on a crisp, dry lager base.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium body, clean and crisp.

children.tryIf: you love IPAs but want the crisp, clean finish of a lager

children.name: Amber Lagers
children.description: Toasty, malt-forward lagers built on Vienna and Munich malts, from amber-orange to copper.

children.name: Vienna Lager
children.description: Moderately strong, reddish-amber lager with a soft, elegant toasty Vienna-malt character, moderate bitterness and a dry finish.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Anton Dreher learned Bavarian bottom fermentation at Spaten in Munich and applied it to paler, English-style kilned malt.

notes.aroma: Toasty, bready Vienna malt with a little floral-spicy hop.
notes.flavor: Soft, elegant toasty malt balanced by moderate bitterness; fairly dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium with a gentle creaminess.

children.tryIf: you like toasted bread and want an amber lager that stays dry and easy

children.name: Märzen (Oktoberfest)
children.description: Elegant, malty, amber-orange to copper German lager with a rich, toasty-bready Munich/Vienna malt depth and a dry, clean finish; the pre-1990 Oktoberfest beer.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: Spaten's 1841 lager was developed alongside Dreher's, and Sedlmayr's amber 1872 Oktoberfest Märzen followed the Vienna model.
BJCP: the Märzen name is older than 1841, and the early March-brewed Bavarian lagers were dark brown.

notes.aroma: Rich bread crust and toasty Munich malt; clean, with very little hop aroma.
notes.flavor: Rich, toasty-bready malt that hints at sweetness but finishes dry; restrained bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium, smooth and creamy; strength well hidden.

children.tryIf: you like toasty, malty amber beer with pretzels and roast chicken

children.name: International Amber Lager
children.description: Smooth, easy-drinking amber mass-market lager with mild caramel/toast malt flavor and low bitterness; may use adjuncts.

parents.note: Generally an amber adaptation of mass-market International Pale Lager.

notes.aroma: Light grain with caramel or toasty accents and faint hops.
notes.flavor: Mild caramel and toast with low bitterness; malty-sweet impression, moderately dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium, smooth; medium to high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want a smooth, easy amber that is a step up in flavor from pale lager

children.name: Czech Amber Lager (Polotmavé)
children.description: Malt-driven amber to copper Czech lager with caramel, toast and bready notes, balanced by spicy Saaz hops; may be fuller or drier depending on brewery.

parents.note: A Vienna-style lager that has continued to be brewed in the Czech lands.

notes.aroma: Rich bready or caramel malt with spicy Saaz hops and maybe plum or berry.
notes.flavor: Complex caramel-toast malt with prominent clean bitterness; finish ranges from dry to sweetish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, soft and round with a gentle creaminess.

children.tryIf: you like caramel and toast but still want a hoppy, bitter balance

children.name: Dark Lagers
children.description: Brown to black lagers, from bready-malty Munich Dunkel to roasty-dry Schwarzbier.

children.name: Munich Dunkel
children.description: Deep copper to dark brown Bavarian lager with a rich, bready-toasty Munich-malt flavor, hints of chocolate or nuts, and a smooth, clean finish.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)
children.yearLabel: 1553 stands for the Bavarian brown-lager tradition (summer-brewing ban); Munich Dunkel itself developed at Spaten in the 1830s (BJCP)

notes.aroma: Toasted bread crust with hints of chocolate, nuts, caramel and toffee.
notes.flavor: Rich, bready-toasty malt with a touch of chocolate, restrained bitterness and a medium-dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, soft and smooth; not heavy.

children.tryIf: you like bread crust and toasted nuts and want a dark beer without roast bitterness

children.name: Schwarzbier
children.description: Very dark, dry German black lager with a soft roast and chocolate character, no harsh burnt flavors, and a crisp lager finish.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)
children.yearLabel: Köstritzer brewing records from 1543 (date approx. for the black-beer tradition); a regional Thuringian/Saxon specialty

notes.aroma: Soft roast, dark chocolate and coffee hints with light malt and a little hop spice.
notes.flavor: Smooth bittersweet-chocolate roast without burnt notes, moderate bitterness and a dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium, smooth and crisp.

children.tryIf: you like dark beers but want something light, dry and crisp

children.name: Czech Dark Lager (Tmavé)
children.description: Rich, dark, malty Czech lager whose roast ranges from barely noticeable to prominent, with caramel and bready notes and a spicy Czech-hop balance.
children.yearLabel: U Fleků brewing since 1499 (date approx. for the dark-beer tradition); bottom-fermented dark lager from the mid-1800s

notes.aroma: Deep malt with caramel, bread crust, cola and dark fruit; roast from faint to moderate.
notes.flavor: Rich, slightly sweet malt with caramel, light chocolate or coffee and a perceptible spicy-hop balance.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full and creamy, but not heavy.

children.tryIf: you like cola, caramel and dark bread and want a rich yet drinkable dark lager

children.name: International Dark Lager
children.description: Dark, smooth, easy-drinking mass-market lager with light caramel and roast, low bitterness and a sweetish finish; may use adjuncts and coloring.
malts: Light use of dark roasted malt

topSellers.name: Negra Modelo
topSellers.brewery: Grupo Modelo (AB InBev; Constellation Brands in US)

parents.note: Darker, coloured or sweetened versions of International Pale Lager from the same industrial breweries.
Also brewed as a more accessible and cheaper version of traditional dark lagers.

notes.aroma: Faint malt with light caramel and roast.
notes.flavor: Mild sweetish malt with hints of caramel, cocoa or molasses; low bitterness, fairly crisp.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium-light with a light creaminess.

children.tryIf: you want a dark beer that is as easy and light as a regular lager

children.name: Bocks
children.description: Strong German lagers, from the pale spring Maibock up to freeze-concentrated Eisbock.

children.name: Helles Bock (Maibock)
children.description: Relatively pale, strong, malty German lager with a bready-toasty Pils/Munich malt character, more hop presence than other bocks, and a dry finish.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)

parents.note: BJCP: a fairly recent pale development within the bock family, served as Maibock in spring.

notes.aroma: Grainy-sweet Pils malt with light toast and spicy-floral hops; a little alcohol.
notes.flavor: Strong bready malt with more hop bitterness than other bocks; well attenuated, moderately dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, smooth; light alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you want a strong golden lager that is malty but not heavy

children.name: Dunkles Bock
children.description: Dark, strong, malty lager with a rich, toasty Munich/Vienna malt character, melanoidin depth and very little hop flavor.
malts: Tiny % dark roasted malt for color
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)
children.yearLabel: 14th century (Einbeck, Hanseatic export); recreated in Munich from the 1600s

notes.aroma: Rich bread crust and toasty Munich malt with a little dark fruit and alcohol.
notes.flavor: Deep toasty malt with dark caramel and a bit of lingering sweetness; low bitterness, no roast.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, smooth; some alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like rich, toasty dark beers and cold-weather warmers

children.name: Doppelbock
children.description: Very strong, rich, malty lager, either golden or (more often) dark, with deep bready-toasty malt, dark-fruit hints, low bitterness and alcohol warmth. Names traditionally end in "-ator".
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70)
children.yearLabel: c.1651 per Paulaner tradition (strong Lenten beer, later 'Salvator'); BJCP: by the 1700s

parents.note: Munich's strong Lenten beer is grouped in the bock family, which Munich had recreated from Einbeck beer in the 1600s; BJCP compares it to a stronger, richer Dunkles Bock.

notes.aroma: Very rich malt with toasted bread, caramel, plum and raisin and some alcohol.
notes.flavor: Intensely malty, sweetish and rich with dark fruit; low bitterness and a smooth, attenuated finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full, very smooth; gentle alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like rich, malty, warming beers that taste like bread pudding and dried fruit

children.name: Eisbock
children.description: Full-bodied, very strong, dark lager made by freezing a doppelbock and removing ice, which concentrates its malt, dark-fruit and alcohol.
children.yeast: Clean German lager yeast (e.g. Weihenstephan W-34/70); then freeze-concentrated

parents.note: Made by freezing a strong bock or doppelbock and removing ice to concentrate it.

notes.aroma: Intense concentrated malt, caramel, plum and grape with clear alcohol.
notes.flavor: Rich, sweet malt and dark fruit balanced by significant alcohol; not cloying.
notes.mouthfeel: Full to very full and silky; low carbonation and strong warmth.

children.tryIf: you sip port or brandy and want a beer for slow sipping

children.name: Hybrid Beers
children.description: Beers that cross ale and lager methods: ales fermented cool and lagered, or lager yeast fermented warm.

children.name: German Hybrids (Obergärig Lagerbier)
children.description: Top-fermented ales from the Rhineland that are cold-conditioned like lagers: Kölsch in Cologne and Altbier in Düsseldorf.

children.name: Kölsch
children.description: Clean, crisp, delicately balanced pale ale from Cologne with a soft grainy-honey malt, faint fruity esters, subtle noble hops and a dry, lagered finish. "Kölsch" is a protected appellation (Kölsch Konvention, 1986), so American versions are labeled "Kölsch-style".
children.yeast: Attenuative, clean Kölsch ale yeast fermented cool (~15 °C), then cold-lagered

parents.note: BJCP: Cologne's top-fermenting brewers developed Kölsch in the late 1800s as an alternative to pale lagers.

notes.aroma: Subtle grainy-honey malt with faint apple or pear and light noble hops.
notes.flavor: Delicate and balanced: soft malt, faint fruit and moderate bitterness; dry, soft finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light; medium to medium-high carbonation and very smooth.

children.tryIf: you want a crisp, delicate, refreshing beer between a lager and a light ale

children.name: Altbier
children.description: Well-balanced, bitter yet malty, clean copper-brown ale from Düsseldorf with a firm, lasting bitterness, rich grainy-toasty malt and a dry, lagered finish.
malts: Touch of chocolate/black malt or roasted wheat
children.yeast: Clean, highly attenuative Altbier ale yeast (e.g. WLP036 / Wyeast 1007), fermented cool then cold-conditioned

children.name: Sticke Alt
children.description: A "secret" seasonal Altbier from Düsseldorf's brewpubs. It is stronger, darker, maltier and more heavily hopped than standard Alt, and often dry-hopped. Uerige also brews a ~8.5% Doppelsticke. The ranges are approximate, because neither BJCP nor BA defines this style.

parents.note: Stronger, hoppier "secret" seasonal version of Düsseldorf Altbier.

notes.aroma: Richer toasty malt and more spicy, herbal hops than regular Alt, often dry-hopped.
notes.flavor: Bigger malt and stronger bitterness than Alt, with a bittersweet, long finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full, smooth; a little alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like Altbier and want a stronger, hoppier special-occasion version

children.yearLabel: 1838 (Schumacher, Düsseldorf); BJCP dates modern Altbier to the late 19th century

notes.aroma: Bready, nutty, toasted bread-crust malt with spicy, peppery hops.
notes.flavor: Rich malt held by firm, long-lasting bitterness; dry, bittersweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, smooth; medium to medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like amber beers with real bitterness and a dry finish

children.name: American Hybrids
children.description: American beers that mix ale and lager techniques: lager yeast at ale temperatures (steam beer), or ales built to compete with lagers (cream ale).

children.name: Cream Ale
children.description: Clean, well-attenuated, highly carbonated pale ale (sometimes blended with lager) with a light corn sweetness and low bitterness. It was created as an ale brewer's answer to light lager.
children.yeast: Clean American ale yeast, or ale/lager blend, fermented cool

topSellers.name: Genesee Cream Ale
topSellers.brewery: Genesee Brewing (North American Breweries; ex-FIFCO USA)

children.yearLabel: second half of the 1800s; survived Prohibition

parents.note: BJCP: a sparkling ale brewed to compete with the lagers of Canada and the US Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest.

notes.aroma: Light corn sweetness, grainy malt and a gentle floral hop.
notes.flavor: Soft grain and corn with low bitterness; crisp, sometimes faintly sweet finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light and crisp, smooth; high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you want a light, easy lawnmower beer with a bit more character than light lager

children.name: California Common (Steam Beer)
children.description: Toasty, caramelly amber beer with firm bitterness and rustic, minty-woody Northern Brewer hops, fermented with lager yeast at warm ale temperatures. "Steam Beer" is an Anchor trademark. The archetype, Anchor Steam, has been out of production since Anchor Brewing closed in July 2023; Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya bought the brewery in May 2024, but brewing had not resumed as of late 2026.
children.yeast: Warm-tolerant lager yeast fermented at 55-60 °F (e.g. WLP810 San Francisco Lager)
children.yearLabel: c.1850 (Gold Rush-era steam beer); Anchor revival 1971

parents.note: BJCP: Gold Rush brewers fermented lager yeast warm in shallow open fermenters for want of refrigeration, improvising on the lager brewing brought by German immigrants.

notes.aroma: Woody, minty-herbal Northern Brewer hops over caramel and toast.
notes.flavor: Toasty, caramel malt with pronounced bitterness and rustic hop flavor; fairly dry, crisp finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body; medium to medium-high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like amber ales with a woody, herbal hop bite

children.name: Specialty Beers
children.description: Beers defined by an added ingredient or process (smoke, wood, fruit, spice, alternative grains or sugars) laid on top of a base style, plus gluten-free, non-alcoholic and experimental beers.

children.name: Smoked Beers
children.description: Beers made with smoked malt, from Bamberg's beechwood Rauchbier to any style given a smoke accent.

children.name: Rauchbier
children.description: Bamberg-style amber Märzen brewed with beechwood-smoked malt: a toasty, malty lager with a smoky (bacon, campfire) character from mild to intense.
children.yearLabel: c.1850 (date approx.): BJCP says the style developed after Märzen; smoked-malt beers much older

parents.note: Bamberg smoked lager built on a Märzen base; BJCP says the style must have developed after Märzen.

notes.aroma: Beechwood smoke (bacon, campfire, ham) over toasty Märzen malt.
notes.flavor: Smoke and rich toasty malt in balance; moderate bitterness, medium-dry finish. Smoke ranges mild to intense.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, smooth lager character.

children.tryIf: you like smoked meats, bacon or peaty whisky

children.name: Classic Style Smoked Beer
children.description: A classic base style such as porter, bock or Helles brewed with smoked malt (beech, oak, alder, fruitwood and others) so the smoke blends harmoniously with the base beer. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

origin.era: Smoked malt pre-1700s; modern revival 1980s+ (e.g. Alaskan Smoked Porter 1988)

malts: Smoked malt (beech, oak, alder, cherry, peat-free)
children.yearLabel: smoked malt traditional; modern revival 1980s+ (Alaskan Smoked Porter 1988)

parents.note: BJCP: craft brewers adapted the German tradition of smoked malt in Rauchbier, Bock, Weissbier, Helles and other styles to many base styles.

notes.aroma: Wood smoke (beech, alder, oak) blended into the base beer; often a porter or bock. Varies with base.
notes.flavor: Base-beer malt and hops with low to assertive smoke; smoke adds dryness. Profile follows the base style.
notes.mouthfeel: Follows the base style, usually medium.

children.tryIf: you like campfire and smoked foods and a familiar beer style underneath

children.name: Specialty Smoked Beer
children.description: A smoked beer built on a base style and also given other specialty ingredients such as fruit, spice, honey, vanilla or barrel aging. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

topSellers.name: Stone Smoked Porter with Vanilla Bean
topSellers.brewery: Stone Brewing (Firestone Walker / Duvel Moortgat USA since 2026)

notes.aroma: Smoke plus extras such as chili, fruit, vanilla or barrel notes; varies widely with base.
notes.flavor: Smoked malt meets the added ingredients over the base beer; balance varies by recipe.
notes.mouthfeel: Follows the base style, usually medium.

children.tryIf: you like smoky flavors combined with something unusual

children.name: Wood & Barrel-Aged Beers
children.description: Beers aged in wood or on wood: neutral oak, or barrels that previously held spirits or wine.

children.name: Wood-Aged Beer
children.description: A base beer aged in wooden barrels or on oak/other wood without a previous alcohol character, picking up vanilla, toast, coconut, caramel or tannin. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

origin.era: Wooden casks were historical norm; modern deliberate wood character 1990s+

adjuncts: Oak chips, staves, spirals or cubes
children.yearLabel: wooden casks traditional; deliberate wood character 1990s+

notes.aroma: Oak, vanilla, toast and coconut over the base beer, often a strong ale or stout; varies with base.
notes.flavor: Base beer plus woody, vanilla and caramel notes and some tannin; profile follows the base.
notes.mouthfeel: Usually medium to full; wood tannins add grip and dryness.

children.tryIf: you like oaky wines or whisky and rich beers with a vanilla edge

children.name: Specialty Wood-Aged Beer (Barrel-Aged)
children.description: A beer aged in barrels that previously held spirits or wine, such as bourbon, rum or port. Imperial stouts in bourbon barrels are the archetype, with vanilla, oak, caramel and boozy-spirit notes. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
malts: Per base style (often imperial stout / barleywine grists)

parents.note: Wood ageing with spirit, wine or other previous barrel contents; BJCP gives it the same history as 33A.

notes.aroma: Bourbon, vanilla, oak, caramel and coconut over roasty stout; varies with spirit and base.
notes.flavor: Rich, sweet and boozy: spirit and oak notes over big roast and malt (in the classic stout version).
notes.mouthfeel: Full and silky with clear alcohol warmth; low carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like bourbon or rum and big desserts in a glass

children.name: Fruit Beers
children.description: Non-sour beers built around fruit, from shandies and fruit wheats to grape-must ales. Fruited lambics, sours and Italian Grape Ale belong to Wild & Sour.

children.name: Fruit Beer
children.description: A base beer with one or more fruits added, where the fruit flavor is clearly noticeable yet balanced with the beer. Radlers and shandies are commercial cousins. BJCP gives no numbers (stats vary with the base style); the ranges shown are the BA "American-Style Fruit Beer" guideline (SRM 5-50 "or color of fruit").

origin.era: Ancient roots; modern US fruit beers 1980s+

malts: Per base style (often pale, wheat or light lager bases)
adjuncts: Fruit, purée, juice or concentrate (e.g. raspberry, cherry, citrus, watermelon)
children.yearLabel: ancient roots; modern craft fruit beers 1980s+

notes.aroma: Clearly fruity (berries, cherry, citrus, stone fruit) over the base beer; varies with fruit and base.
notes.flavor: Fruit flavor in balance with the beer; often dry, as fruit sugars ferment out. Varies widely.
notes.mouthfeel: Often lighter than the base beer; dark fruits can add light tannin.

children.tryIf: you like fruit and want a beer that is fruity but still tastes like beer

children.name: Fruit and Spice Beer
children.description: A beer with both fruit and spices, herbs or vegetables, which blend with each other and the base beer. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

notes.aroma: Fruit and spice together, such as cherry-cinnamon or orange-coriander; varies widely.
notes.flavor: Fruit and spice blend over the base beer with low bitterness; balance depends on the recipe.
notes.mouthfeel: Usually light to medium; fruit lightens, some spices add warmth.

children.tryIf: you like mulled wine, spiced fruit desserts or flavored teas

children.name: Grape Ale
children.description: BJCP 2021's general grape-must category: a relatively neutral pale beer co-fermented with grape must (typically 15-20% of the grist) for a dry, sparkling-wine-like character; not sour or Brett-funky. It grew out of Italian Grape Ale, which BJCP keeps as a separate local style (X3, broader ranges) and which this dataset lists under Wild & Sour.
children.yeast: Fruity-spicy ale yeast or neutral/wine yeast

parents.note: The Italian Grape Ale, published by BJCP in 2015, inspired many local variations in other countries.

notes.aroma: Varietal grape (white-wine, stone fruit or red berry) over a clean pale-malt base.
notes.flavor: Sparkling-wine-like grape flavor with mild tartness, low bitterness and a very dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium, highly carbonated, crisp.

children.tryIf: you like Prosecco, Champagne or dry white wine

children.name: Spice, Herb & Flavored Beers
children.description: Beers flavored with spices, herbs, vegetables, chiles, coffee, chocolate or honey, including the seasonal pumpkin and winter beers.

children.name: Spice, Herb, or Vegetable Beer
children.description: A base beer showcasing spices, herbs or vegetables (heather, ginger, jasmine, botanicals) in harmony with the underlying style. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

notes.aroma: The spice, herb or vegetable (ginger, heather, botanicals) shows over the base beer; varies widely.
notes.flavor: Spice or herb flavor in balance with the base beer; some add bitterness or warmth.
notes.mouthfeel: Follows the base style; usually medium.

children.tryIf: you like herbal teas, gin botanicals or spiced cooking

children.name: Pumpkin / Autumn Seasonal Beer
children.description: An amber to copper, malty seasonal beer with "pumpkin pie" spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, clove, ginger), often with pumpkin or squash and brown sugar or molasses. BJCP 30B gives no numbers; the ranges shown are the BA "Pumpkin Spice Beer" guideline (BA also lists an unspiced Pumpkin/Squash Beer).
children.yearLabel: 1985 (Buffalo Bill's Pumpkin Ale); colonial pumpkin beers earlier

notes.aroma: Pumpkin-pie spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, clove, ginger) over toasty, caramel malt.
notes.flavor: Malty and spiced, like pie crust and brown sugar; low bitterness and a fairly full finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full; may be slightly warming.

children.tryIf: you like pumpkin pie, spiced lattes and fall flavors

children.name: Winter Seasonal Beer
children.description: A stronger, darker, warming holiday beer with Christmas spices, citrus peel or dried fruit, and malty, caramel-rich depth. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

origin.era: Traditional winter ales; Anchor Christmas Ale 1975

children.yeast: Ale or lager yeast per base
children.yearLabel: traditional winter ales; modern spiced category from Anchor Our Special Ale, 1975

notes.aroma: Malty, spicy and fruity: cinnamon, clove, orange peel and dried fruit over caramel malt.
notes.flavor: Rich, sweetish malt with holiday spice and dried fruit; restrained bitterness, warming finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full, often chewy; alcohol warmth.

children.tryIf: you like fruitcake, mulled wine and gingerbread

children.name: Chile Beer
children.description: A beer flavored with chile peppers, with green-vegetal or fruity pepper flavor and heat ranging from subtle to fiery. BA calls it "Chili Pepper Beer". Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
malts: Per base style (often light lager, pale ale or stout)
adjuncts: Chile peppers (jalapeño, habanero, serrano, chipotle, ghost)

topSellers.name: Xocoveza
topSellers.brewery: Stone Brewing (Firestone Walker / Duvel Moortgat USA since 2026)

notes.aroma: Green, vegetal or fruity chile pepper over the base beer; heat ranges mild to fiery. Varies with base.
notes.flavor: Pepper flavor and capsaicin heat over the base beer, often a pale ale or lager.
notes.mouthfeel: Follows the base style; heat builds on the palate.

children.tryIf: you like spicy food, jalapeños or a spicy margarita

children.name: Coffee Beer
children.description: A beer, most often a stout or porter, flavored with coffee beans or cold brew so that roast-coffee aroma and flavor stand out. Pale "golden coffee" versions also exist. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
malts: Per base style (often roasted barley, chocolate malt, oats)
adjuncts: Coffee (whole bean, cold brew or espresso)

notes.aroma: Fresh roasted coffee, often over a stout or porter with chocolate notes; pale versions exist.
notes.flavor: Coffee and roast lead, with dark malt and some bitterness; varies with base beer.
notes.mouthfeel: Usually medium to full and smooth (in stout and porter versions).

children.tryIf: you drink your coffee black or love espresso

children.name: Chocolate Beer
children.description: A beer, usually dark, flavored with chocolate, cocoa or cacao nibs for a clear chocolate character beyond what dark malts provide. BA calls it "Chocolate or Cocoa Beer". Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

notes.aroma: Cocoa and dark chocolate over roasty dark malt, sometimes with vanilla.
notes.flavor: Chocolate and roast with a sweetish, dessert-like palate; usually stout or porter based.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full, often silky and smooth.

children.tryIf: you like dark chocolate, brownies or mocha

children.name: Honey Beer
children.description: A beer brewed with honey so that its floral, sweet-aromatic honey character is noticeable, often with a drier body because honey ferments out completely. BJCP files it under 31B Alternative Sugar. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
children.yeast: Ale or lager yeast per base
adjuncts: Honey (clover, orange blossom, heather and others)

notes.aroma: Floral honey aroma over the base beer; the type of honey shapes it. Varies with base.
notes.flavor: Light honey flavor that often finishes drier than expected, as honey ferments fully.
notes.mouthfeel: Light to medium, often a little drier than the base beer.

children.tryIf: you like honey, mead or floral flavors

children.name: Alternative & Other Specialty
children.description: Beers defined by alternative ingredients or processes: other grains and sugars, gluten-free, non-alcoholic and experimental.

children.name: Alternative Grain Beer
children.description: A base style brewed with a noticeable share of a non-standard grain, such as rye, buckwheat, spelt, millet, sorghum or rice, which adds its own flavor and texture. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
malts: Alternative grain (rye, spelt, buckwheat, oats, millet, sorghum)

notes.aroma: Base beer plus a grainy, nutty or earthy note from rye, buckwheat, spelt, oats or others.
notes.flavor: Same as the base beer with extra grainy, nutty or spicy grain flavor; varies with grain.
notes.mouthfeel: Oats and rye add body and silkiness; gluten-free grains can thin it.

children.tryIf: you like whole-grain bread and nutty flavors

children.name: Alternative Sugar Beer
children.description: A base beer with a noticeable sugar adjunct, such as maple syrup, molasses, piloncillo, candi syrup or agave, that adds flavor beyond fermentables. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

notes.aroma: Maple, molasses, agave, candi or piloncillo notes over the base beer; varies with sugar.
notes.flavor: Base beer plus the sugar’s own flavor; some finish dry, others fuller and sweeter.
notes.mouthfeel: Follows the base beer; body rises or falls with the sugar used.

children.tryIf: you like maple syrup, molasses or brown-sugar flavors

children.name: Gluten-Free Beer
children.description: A beer made only from gluten-free ingredients (sorghum, millet, buckwheat, rice, corn and others) and often imitating a classic style. BA puts gluten-reduced barley beers in their base style, not here. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.
hops: Per target style (Cascade, Saaz and others)

notes.aroma: Usually mimics a pale ale or lager; sorghum or millet can add a fruity, slightly tart note.
notes.flavor: Lighter malt flavor than barley beers, sometimes a light tang; varies with base and grains.
notes.mouthfeel: Often lighter and thinner than barley-based beers.

children.tryIf: you need a gluten-free beer and want something close to a familiar style

children.name: Non-Alcoholic Beer
children.description: A beer that imitates any style with less than 0.5% ABV, made by dealcoholization, arrested or limited fermentation, or special yeast; quality has risen sharply since 2018. BA calls it "Non-Alcohol Malt Beverage".
hops: Per target style (often heavy late hopping for NA IPAs)
children.yeast: Maltose-negative yeast, arrested fermentation, or dealcoholized after normal fermentation

notes.aroma: Usually lager or IPA-like: grainy malt and hops, sometimes a worty note. Varies with style.
notes.flavor: Imitates its base style with less complexity; can taste slightly sweet or worty.
notes.mouthfeel: Usually light; lacks alcohol warmth and can feel a little thin.

children.tryIf: you want the taste of beer with no alcohol

children.name: Experimental Beer
children.description: A catch-all for beers that fit no other style: unusual ingredients, processes or fermentation, including "extreme" freeze-concentrated or ancient-recipe beers. Stats vary with the base style. The ranges shown are a typical envelope, not a guideline limit.

notes.aroma: Anything goes: unusual ingredients, processes or fermentation; there is no typical profile.
notes.flavor: Varies completely; judge each beer on whether its idea works and tastes good.
notes.mouthfeel: Varies with the beer.

children.tryIf: you are adventurous and want to try something no style covers

children.name: Historical & Regional
children.description: Extinct, revived and living folk beers, from medieval German and Dutch ales to Nordic farmhouse brews and indigenous beers around the world.

children.name: German & Central European Historical
children.description: Revived or surviving old-world styles from Germany, Poland and the Low Countries: smoked and sour wheat beers, oat beers, steam and stone beers.

children.name: Lichtenhainer
children.description: A sour, smoked, low-gravity wheat beer from Thuringia. It is complex yet refreshing, with moderate lactic tartness, a light smoke and very low bitterness, much like a pre-1840 Berliner Weisse.

notes.aroma: Dry wood smoke over bread, with lemon and green apple and a light sour note.
notes.flavor: Clean lactic tartness and medium smoke with lemony fruit; very low bitterness and dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light; tingly acidity and high carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like Berliner Weisse and smoky flavors and want both in one glass

children.name: Piwo Grodziskie (Grätzer)
children.description: A low-gravity, highly carbonated, bitter Polish wheat beer made from oak-smoked wheat malt. It has a clean fermentation and no sourness. It is known in German as Grätzer and nicknamed "Polish champagne".
children.yeast: Clean, attenuative ale yeast (historically a multi-strain top-fermenter); not Weizen yeast

notes.aroma: Gentle oak smoke with light herbal-spicy hops and a hint of wheat and apple.
notes.flavor: Light oak smoke and clearly bitter finish over thin wheat malt; dry, crisp, no sourness.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body; very high carbonation, champagne-like.

children.tryIf: you want a very low-alcohol, bitter, lightly smoky beer that is still refreshing

children.name: Broyhan
children.description: A pale, top-fermented wheat-and-barley beer from Hanover, first brewed by Cord Broyhan in 1526 and made until about 1919, with a light, slightly sweet-sour character. Recent revivals sometimes add botanicals. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.
children.yeast: Top-fermenting ale yeast, sometimes with lactic souring

notes.aroma: Pale wheat and barley malt with a mild sour note; modern revivals may add spices.
notes.flavor: Light, gently sweet-and-sour with low bitterness. Historical accounts differ, so versions vary.
notes.mouthfeel: Light and refreshing; moderate carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like Berliner Weisse or Gose and are curious about lost German beers

children.name: Adambier
children.description: A strong, dark, hoppy old Dortmund ale, traditionally long-aged in wood and sometimes slightly sour or lightly smoky, with toast, caramel and dark-fruit notes. Stats are the BA "Adambier" guideline.

origin.era: Medieval roots; died out by mid-1900s; revived 1994 (Hair of the Dog)

children.yearLabel: pre-lager Dortmund ale (documented 1800s); revived 1994 (Hair of the Dog)

notes.aroma: Toast, caramel and dark fruit with oak and sometimes light smoke or tartness.
notes.flavor: Strong and malty with dark fruit, firm hop bitterness and, from wood aging, mild sourness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full; warming alcohol.

children.tryIf: you like old ales, barleywines or Flanders browns

children.name: Dampfbier
children.description: A Bavarian Forest "steam beer": an amber, all-barley ale fermented warm with Weizen-type yeast, giving fruity-phenolic notes. It was named for the bubbling ("steaming") fermentation. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.
children.yeast: Bavarian Weizen ale yeast fermented warm

notes.aroma: Bread and light caramel with banana and clove from weizen yeast.
notes.flavor: Malty amber barley ale with fruity-phenolic yeast; low bitterness and a fairly dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body; lively carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like Dunkelweizen and want a barley-based, amber version

children.name: Zoigl
children.description: An unfiltered, young, amber-gold lager brewed in the communal brewhouses (Kommunbrauhäuser) of the Upper Palatinate and served only in the brewers' own Zoiglstuben, which open in rotation on a published calendar, signaled by a hanging six-pointed star. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

origin.country: Germany (Upper Palatinate: Windischeschenbach, Neuhaus, Falkenberg, Mitterteich, Eslarn)

children.yeast: Bottom-fermenting lager yeast, cool-fermented in household cellars

notes.aroma: Fresh bread and grainy malt with spicy noble hops and a yeasty note.
notes.flavor: Malty, rustic and fresh like a Kellerbier, with moderate bitterness; recipes vary by brewer.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, soft and unfiltered; often gently carbonated.

children.tryIf: you like Kellerbier and the idea of drinking fresh beer in a village pub

children.name: Steinbier
children.description: A "stone beer" boiled by dropping red-hot greywacke or granite stones into the wort. The stones caramelize sugars, and they are then added back during maturation for a smoky-caramel, toffee character. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

origin.era: Pre-modern (no metal kettles); revived 1982 by Rauchenfels (since retired), today Leikeim and Hofstetten

notes.aroma: Caramelized sugar, toffee and a light smoky note from hot stones.
notes.flavor: Toffee-caramel malt with a hint of smoke and low bitterness; slightly sweet.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body, smooth.

children.tryIf: you like toffee, crème brûlée and a whisper of smoke

children.name: Mumme (Brunswick Mum)
children.description: A thick, near-black, sweet, strong ale from Braunschweig that was exported widely by sea in the 1500s-1700s. Today it survives mainly as a non-alcoholic malt extract; Nettelbeck's revived Mumme beer has reportedly ended production, and the name lives on in Scandinavian Christmas beers. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.
adjuncts: Historically herbs and spices (fir/birch tips in some recipes)

notes.aroma: Molasses, dark bread and dried fruit over dark malt.
notes.flavor: Very malty and sweet like malt extract or treacle, with little bitterness; versions vary greatly.
notes.mouthfeel: Thick and full, syrupy in traditional form.

children.tryIf: you like molasses, malt loaf or sweet dark beers

children.name: Kuit / Kuyt / Koyt
children.description: A medieval Dutch oat beer: gold to copper, grainy-bready, lightly hopped and sometimes gruit-spiced. Under BA rules the grist is at least 45% oats and 20% wheat; stats are the BA "Dutch-Style Kuit, Kuyt or Koyt" guideline (Jopen Koyt, at 8.5%, is stronger than the BA range).
adjuncts: Optional gruit herbs (bog myrtle and others)

notes.aroma: Grainy-bready oat and wheat malt with light noble hops.
notes.flavor: Soft grainy-bready malt and moderate bitterness; clean, lightly fruity, dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Low to medium, with silky oat smoothness.

children.tryIf: you like oat and wheat beers and medieval brewing history

children.name: Nordic & Baltic Farmhouse Ales
children.description: Raw-ale traditions from Finland, Gotland, Norway and Estonia: juniper, home-smoked malt, farmhouse yeast (kveik) and often no boil.

children.name: Sahti
children.description: A sweet, heavy, strong Finnish farmhouse ale, usually with rye and juniper, a banana-clove yeast character and little or no hops. The wort is often unboiled and filtered through juniper twigs in a kuurna trough.

origin.era: At least 500 years; EU TSG protected 2002

children.yeast: Finnish baker's yeast, warm and fast (Weizen yeast as substitute)
children.yearLabel: at least 500 years (Finnish farmhouse tradition); EU TSG 2002

notes.aroma: Sweet worty malt with high banana, clove and woody juniper; rye in the background.
notes.flavor: Fairly sweet raw-malt flavor with caramel, banana and clove and a piney juniper touch; no hops.
notes.mouthfeel: Thick, heavy and almost still; warming.

children.tryIf: you like sweet, rustic, strong beers and juniper or gin

children.name: Gotlandsdricka
children.description: A Gotland (Sweden) farmhouse ale brewed with birch-smoked malt and juniper-infused water. It is smoky, piney-resinous and sweetish, sometimes with honey, and fermented with baker's or farmhouse yeast. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.
children.yearLabel: medieval / Viking-age roots (approx.); living farmhouse tradition

notes.aroma: Birch smoke, juniper and sweet malt, sometimes honey.
notes.flavor: Smoky, piney-resinous and sweetish with farmhouse-yeast fruit and little bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium body; low carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like smoky and herbal flavors and rustic farmhouse beers

children.name: Stjørdalsøl
children.description: A Norwegian farmhouse ale from the Stjørdal valley, made from home-malted barley kilned in smoke-filled "såinnhus" kilns. It is intensely smoky, juniper-tinged and often fermented with kveik. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

origin.era: Living farmhouse tradition (more than 400 home brewers)

notes.aroma: Intense wood smoke with juniper and fruity kveik yeast.
notes.flavor: Heavily smoky malt with fruity yeast, a little sweetness and minimal hops.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full; often low carbonation.

children.tryIf: you love peaty whisky and strongly smoked flavors

children.name: Koduõlu
children.description: An Estonian farmhouse ("home") ale, strongest on Saaremaa and Muhu islands: unboiled, naturally carbonated, hazy, sweetish and juniper-scented, with fruity, rustic farmhouse-yeast character; usually 6-9% ABV. Almost all is home-brewed; Pihtla on Saaremaa is the main commercial producer. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

notes.aroma: Juniper and sweet grain with fruity, rustic farmhouse yeast.
notes.flavor: Sweetish and malty with juniper and fruity yeast; very low bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to full, hazy and soft; light natural carbonation.

children.tryIf: you like Sahti or rustic, sweet farmhouse ales

children.name: Anglo-American Historical
children.description: Extinct or nearly extinct styles from 1800s Britain and pre-Prohibition America.

children.name: Kentucky Common
children.description: A clean, dry, refreshing, slightly malty dark saloon beer from Louisville. It is mild, with light toast and caramel and high carbonation, and was served very fresh.
children.yearLabel: after the Civil War (c. 1865) until Prohibition

notes.aroma: Grainy-corn sweetness with light toast and caramel and floral hops.
notes.flavor: Mild grainy malt with light caramel and toast and medium-low bitterness; fairly dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-light, soft and highly carbonated.

children.tryIf: you want a dark-colored beer that is light, dry and easy

children.name: Pre-Prohibition Lager
children.description: A bitter, hoppy pale American adjunct lager, the German-immigrant "Classic American Pilsner", often with a robust corn flavor, more body and far more hops than modern American lager.
children.yearLabel: mid-1800s (date approx.); most popular from the 1870s until 1919; homebrew revival 1990s

parents.note: BJCP: an adaptation of continental pale lagers by immigrant German brewers using native six-row barley, corn or rice and American hops.

notes.aroma: Grainy malt, corn sweetness and rustic floral-spicy hops.
notes.flavor: Grainy-corn malt with substantial clean bitterness and hop flavor; dry finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium to medium-full and creamy; well carbonated.

children.tryIf: you like American lager history and want a pilsner with real hop bite

children.name: Burton Ale
children.description: The strong, sweetish, dark-amber to brown ale that made Burton-upon-Trent famous before IPA (Bass No. 1, Ind Coope). It is rich and fruity with a firm hop bitterness, and later survived as winter warmers. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.
children.yearLabel: late 1700s (Baltic trade), then domestic through the 1900s

notes.aroma: Rich caramel and toffee malt with dark fruit and earthy English hops.
notes.flavor: Strong, sweetish and fruity with firm bitterness; warming finish.
notes.mouthfeel: Medium-full to full; warming alcohol.

children.tryIf: you like English old ales, barleywines or winter warmers

children.name: World Traditional & Indigenous
children.description: Living folk beers outside the European brewing mainstream, made from rye bread or sorghum, often low in alcohol and sour.

children.name: Kvass
children.description: A traditional Slavic and Baltic low-alcohol fermented drink of rye bread or rye malt. It is sweet-tart, bready and sometimes flavored with mint or raisins, and is sold in bulk from street tankers and in PET bottles. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

notes.aroma: Dark rye bread crust with a sweet-tart tang; sometimes mint or raisin.
notes.flavor: Sweet and lightly sour, like liquid rye bread; almost no alcohol or bitterness.
notes.mouthfeel: Light body, softly carbonated.

children.tryIf: you like rye bread, sweet-tart drinks or soda alternatives

children.name: Sorghum Beer (Umqombothi / Opaque Beer)
children.description: A traditional Southern and Central African opaque, sour, porridge-like beer of malted sorghum and maize (umqombothi), drunk while still fermenting. Industrial versions sell in "shake shake" cartons, and clear sorghum lagers are a modern offshoot. No BJCP or BA ranges exist, so the ranges are approximate, taken from historical accounts and modern examples.

origin.country: Southern & Central Africa (South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Malawi, Uganda)

hops: None (traditional); light hopping in sorghum lagers
children.yeast: Wild/mixed yeast and Lactobacillus (traditional); commercial ale or lager yeast

topSellers.name: Chibuku Shake Shake
topSellers.brewery: Delta Beverages and other AB InBev affiliates

notes.aroma: Sour porridge, grain and yeast.
notes.flavor: Tart, grainy and yeasty, like thin sour porridge; still fermenting when served.
notes.mouthfeel: Thick, gritty and opaque; lightly fizzy.

children.tryIf: you are curious about traditional African brewing and like sour, grainy drinks
